definition_zh: 丛林；密林；混乱拥挤之处
definition_en: a thick tropical forest full of tangled plants, or any place that feels crowded and without rules
core_image: 藤蔓从地面爬到树冠，脚下连一步平地都找不到
scene: 雨还没停，树叶上滴着水，道路在十米之外就完全消失了。 The path vanished into the jungle after the first bend.
sceneCN: 这里 jungle 是「丛林」（第 1 个义项：热带浓密树林），句意为路拐过第一个弯就消失在丛林里。画面里的物件：藤蔓、树冠、积水。

pos.zh: 名词：丛林；密林；混乱竞争之地

collocations.phrase: cut a path through the jungle

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「丛林般的」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「被丛林覆盖的」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「长满丛林的」

senses.title: Thick tropical forest
senses.definition: a forest in a hot wet region where plants grow so thickly that movement is hard
senses.definitionCN: 炎热潮湿地区树木藤蔓密到难以行走的森林
senses.example: Tigers still live in these jungles.
senses.exampleCN: 这些丛林里仍有老虎生活。
senses.why: The geographic sense is the one the word was borrowed for.
senses.whyCN: 地理义正是这个词被借进英语时所指的。

senses.title: A wild, crowded place
senses.definition: a place or situation that feels crowded, lawless, and hard to survive
senses.definitionCN: 拥挤、缺少规则、难以生存的地方或处境
senses.example: The market at noon is a jungle of carts and shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 中午的市场是一片推车与叫喊的丛林。
senses.why: The metaphor uses the forest to talk about crowded, ruleless human places.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借森林来说拥挤、少规则的人间场所。

senses.title: A mess of things
senses.definition: a confused mass of objects or words
senses.definitionCN: 一堆纠缠不清的物件或文字
senses.example: The report is a jungle of numbers and abbreviations.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是一团数字与缩写的丛林。
senses.why: The mess sense is the metaphor pushed toward pure confusion.
senses.whyCN: 「杂乱」义是这个比喻推到纯粹的混乱那一端。

intro.en: Jungle came from Hindi jangal, "waste land, forest", which goes back to Sanskrit jangala, "dry ground".
intro.cn: jungle 来自印地语 jangal「荒地、森林」，更早是梵语 jangala「干燥之地」。

items.en: jangala meant "dry, arid land".
items.cn: jangala 意为「干燥荒芜之地」。

items.en: jangal named waste or uncultivated land, often wooded.
items.cn: jangal 指荒废未耕种之地，常长着树。

items.en: English in India used jungle for dense Indian forest.
items.cn: 在印度的英国人用 jungle 指印度浓密森林。

items.en: The word entered general English in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词在十九世纪进入普通英语。

items.en: Kipling and later writing fixed the tropical image.
items.cn: 吉卜林及其后的作品固定了热带丛林的意象。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the jun-/jung- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for dense wild growth.
note.cn: 形近组共用 jun-/jung- 开头；近义组收表示浓密野生植被的词。

entries.definition: Like a jungle, thick and wild.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「丛林般的」，同族词。

entries.definition: A confused mixture of things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「杂乱的一堆」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: A harsh ringing of metal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「刺耳声响」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: A dense tropical forest with heavy rain.
Land untouched by people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「荒野」，无人居住。

entries.definition: A mass of bushes growing close together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「灌木丛」，规模较小。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the word back from tropical film scenes to a Sanskrit adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它从热带电影画面追到梵语形容词。

normal.en: Hindi jangal meant waste or wooded land.
normal.cn: 印地语 jangal 指荒地或有树林的地。

normal.en: Sanskrit jangala meant dry ground.
normal.cn: 梵语 jangala 意为干燥之地。

normal.en: Dry land became wet forest in the English image.
normal.cn: 干燥之地在英语的意象里成了潮湿森林。

normal.en: Jungle law is survival without rules.
normal.cn: jungle law 就是没有规则的生存。

normal.en: A concrete jungle has trees of steel.
normal.cn: 水泥丛林里长的是钢铁做的树。

abstract.en: A jungle is a forest that says no to roads.
abstract.cn: 丛林是一片对道路说不的森林。

abstract.en: Where the vines meet, the ground disappears.
abstract.cn: 藤蔓相接的地方，地面就消失了。

abstract.en: Every crowded market is a small jungle.
abstract.cn: 每个拥挤的市场都是一小片丛林。

examples.en: The village sits at the edge of a thick jungle.
examples.cn: 这个村子坐落在浓密丛林的边上。

examples.en: New staff soon learn the jungle of office politics.
examples.cn: 新员工很快就摸清了办公室政治的丛林。

examples.en: The notebook was a jungle of arrows and odd words.
examples.cn: 那本笔记是一团箭头和怪词组成的丛林。

dict_mnemonic.text: jangal（印地语「荒地、树林」）—— 密到走不动的森林

root: 梵语 jangala「干燥之地」→ 印地语 jangal「荒地；树林」→ 英印英语 jungle → 现代英语 jungle。同族有 jungly、jungled。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: tropical thick forest, a crowded lawless place, and a tangled mess.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：热带密林、拥挤无规则之地，以及杂乱的一团。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vines climbing from soil to canopy with no flat ground left.
core.cn: 核心意象：藤蔓从地面爬到树冠，脚下没有平地。

branches.en: THE PATH: a route that vanishes after one bend.
branches.cn: 小径这条线：拐过一个弯就消失的路。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a crowd where rules seem absent.
branches.cn: 市场这条线：规则像是缺席的人群。

branches.en: THE REPORT: numbers and arrows tangled together.
branches.cn: 报告这条线：数字与箭头缠成一团。

branches.en: THE SURVIVAL: both senses test who can keep going.
branches.cn: 生存这条线：两个义项都在考验谁能走下去。

branches.en: THE MESS: crowding and tangling are the same picture.
branches.cn: 杂乱这条线：拥挤与纠缠是同一幅画。

intro.en: Jungle is borrowed from Hindi as a whole; only English endings are added.
intro.cn: jungle 是从印地语整体借来的，只有后面加的英语词尾属于英语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the word is Indic, so latinEntries stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语来源，是印度语系词，所以 latinEntries 留空。

items.exampleCN: 英语写作 jungle，而非 jangal。

items.example: It forms jungled, covered with jungle.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 jungled，被丛林覆盖的。

items.example: It forms jungle cat and jungle law.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 jungle cat 与 jungle law。

items.example: A look-alike with a different origin.

definition_zh: 一集；一段经历；发作期
definition_en: one part of a series, or a single event in a longer story
core_image: 一条长线被分成几段，每段都有自己的开头和结尾
scene: 这部纪录片的第三集讲的是深海生物。 The third episode of the documentary looks at deep-sea life.
sceneCN: 这里 episode 是「一集」（第 1 个义项：系列节目中的一个部分）；句意：这部纪录片的第三集讲的是深海生物。

senses.title: One part of a series
senses.definition: one program in a television or radio series
senses.definitionCN: 电视或广播系列节目中的一期
senses.example: The final episode answered every question.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一集回答了所有疑问。
senses.why: Greek epeisodion meant an interlude between choral songs, and a single part of a series keeps that sense of a bounded section.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 epeisodion 指合唱之间的插段，系列中的一个部分保留了「有边界的段落」这一含义。

senses.title: A single event in a longer story
senses.definition: one event or period within a longer series of events
senses.definitionCN: 较长事件序列中的一个事件或时期
senses.example: That summer was a strange episode in his life.
senses.exampleCN: 那个夏天是他人生中一段奇怪的经历。
senses.why: A bounded section of a story becomes a bounded event in a life.
senses.whyCN: 故事中有边界的一段，变成人生中有边界的一个事件。

senses.title: A period of illness
senses.definition: a short period when a disease or condition is active
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或症状活跃的一段短时期
senses.example: She had a brief episode of dizziness.
senses.exampleCN: 她有过一小段眩晕发作。
senses.why: Medical use treats a bout of illness as a separate section of time.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法把一次病情发作视为一段独立的时间。

intro.en: Episode comes from Greek epeisodion, an addition or interlude, from epi-, upon, and eisodos, a coming in.
intro.cn: episode 来自希腊语 epeisodion（附加段、插曲），由 epi-（在上）与 eisodos（进入）构成。

items.en: Eisodos means a coming in or entrance.
items.cn: eisodos 意为进入、入场。

items.en: Epeisodion means an added interlude.
items.cn: epeisodion 意为附加的插段。

items.en: The word names a section between choral songs.
items.cn: 这个词指合唱歌曲之间的段落。

items.en: French épisode applies it to a part of a story.
items.cn: 法语 épisode 把它用于故事的一部分。

items.en: Modern English uses episode for series parts, events, and bouts of illness.
items.cn: 现代英语用 episode 指剧集、事件和病情发作。

note.en: Episode is a section word, linked to episodic forms and to words for parts of a whole.
note.cn: episode 是表示「段落」的词，与 episodic 词族以及表示整体之部分的词相邻。

entries.definition: made up of separate parts
in separate parts
episodic
one part of a story released in stages
a main division of a book
a single event

normalIntro.en: Episode is a self-contained section: a show part, a life event, or a bout of illness.
normalIntro.cn: episode 是一个自成一体的段落：一集节目、一段人生经历，或一次病情发作。

normal.en: A TV series is made of episodes.
normal.cn: 电视剧由一集一集的 episode 组成。

normal.en: The first episode introduces the main characters.
normal.cn: 第一集介绍主要人物。

normal.en: A brief episode of rain passed quickly.
normal.cn: 一阵短暂的降雨很快过去了。

normal.en: The adjective episodic means made of separate parts.
normal.cn: 形容词 episodic 意为由分开的部分组成。

normal.en: Compare chapter: chapter is for books, episode suits shows and events.
normal.cn: 对比 chapter：chapter 用于书，episode 适用于节目和事件。

abstract.en: Picture a long ribbon cut into neat sections.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长丝带被剪成整齐的几段。

abstract.en: Imagine a door opening onto one scene and closing again.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门打开呈现一幕，然后又关上。

abstract.en: Think of a short storm passing over a calm sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一场短促的暴风雨掠过平静的海面。

examples.en: We watched the opening episode together.
examples.cn: 我们一起看了开篇那一集。

examples.en: The trip was a happy episode in her childhood.
examples.cn: 那次旅行是她童年中一段快乐的经历。

examples.en: He described a sudden episode of back pain.
examples.cn: 他描述了一次突然发作的背痛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「epi + sode」——一段插进来的小故事，就是一集；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 epi-（在上）＋ eisodos（进入）→ epeisodion（插段）→ 法语 épisode → 英语 episode，核心义「整体中的一个段落」。

sensesIntro.en: Episode starts as an interlude, then becomes one part of a series, a single life event, and a bout of illness.
sensesIntro.cn: episode 从插段开始，随后指系列中的一集、人生中的一个事件，以及一次病情发作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long line divided into bounded sections.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长线被分成有边界的段落。

branches.en: One part of a series is the everyday media sense.
branches.cn: 系列中的一集是日常媒体义项。

branches.en: A single event is a section of a life story.
branches.cn: 单个事件是人生故事中的一个段落。

branches.en: A bout of illness is a bounded period of time.
branches.cn: 病情发作是一段有边界的时间。

branches.en: Both a show part and a life event have a clear beginning and end.
branches.cn: 一集节目与一段经历都有清楚的起点和终点。

branches.en: An illness episode is also an event in a person's history.
branches.cn: 一次发病也是个人经历中的一个事件。

intro.en: Episode comes from Greek roots, and English adds the adjective and adverb endings -ic and -ally.
intro.cn: episode 来自希腊语词根，英语再加上形容词与副词词尾 -ic 和 -ally。

latinIntro.en: Greek epi- means upon, and eisodos means a coming in.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 epi- 意为在上，eisodos 意为进入。

items.example: Episodically means from time to time.

definition_zh: 良心；良知；内疚
definition_en: the inner sense of what is right and wrong in your own behaviour
core_image: 深夜独坐，心里有个声音在轻声责备自己
scene: 他把多找的零钱还回去，才觉得心里安稳。 His conscience would not let him keep the money.
sceneCN: 这里 conscience 指「良心」（第 1 个义项：内心判断是非的能力）；句意是良心不容他把这笔钱留下。

senses.title: The inner judge
senses.definition: the inner sense of right and wrong in your own actions
senses.definitionCN: 内心对自己行为是非的判断力
senses.example: Her conscience told her to confess.
senses.exampleCN: 她的良心叫她坦白。
senses.why: No witness is needed when the judge lives inside you.
senses.whyCN: 当法官住在你心里，就不需要别的证人。

senses.title: A feeling of guilt
senses.definition: a feeling of guilt about something you have done
senses.definitionCN: 对自己做过的事感到有罪的不安
senses.example: He had a guilty conscience for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 他内疚了好几个星期。
senses.why: A wrong act keeps sending its bill back to the same desk.
senses.whyCN: 做错的事会把账单一次次送回同一张桌子。

senses.title: Moral principle
senses.definition: a shared moral sense that guides what people support
senses.definitionCN: 引导人们支持什么的一种共同道义感
senses.example: The vote was a matter of conscience, not of party.
senses.exampleCN: 这次投票是良知问题，而不是党派问题。
senses.why: Some choices are made by a whole person, not by a side.
senses.whyCN: 有些选择由整个人做出，而不是由某个阵营做出。

intro.en: Conscience comes from Latin conscientia, knowledge shared with oneself, from com-, with, and scire, to know.
intro.cn: conscience 来自拉丁语 conscientia，意为与自己共知，由 com-（与）与 scire（知道）构成。

items.en: Scire meant to know or to understand.
items.cn: scire 意为知道或明白。

items.en: Conscire meant to know something together with another.
items.cn: conscire 意为与另一个人共同知道某事。

items.en: Conscientia also meant knowing with yourself, hence a private judge.
items.cn: conscientia 也表示与自己共知，由此成为内心的审判者。

items.en: Old French conscience carried the moral sense.
items.cn: 古法语 conscience 承载了道德含义。

items.en: English conscience meant the inward knowledge of good and evil.
items.cn: 英语 conscience 指内心对善恶的认识。

items.en: It now also names the unease you feel after doing wrong.
items.cn: 如今它也指做错事后感到的不安。

note.en: The look-alike group is the conscious family, often mixed up with this word, and the meaning group names related moral ideas.
note.cn: 形近组是与它常被混淆的 conscious 家族，近义组列出相关的道德概念。

entries.definition: awake and aware of what is around you
the state of being awake and aware
careful to do what is right and proper
beliefs about right and wrong behaviour
the bad feeling of having done wrong
a doubt that stops you doing something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a voice in a quiet room, then move to the bill you cannot refuse and to a vote made alone.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从安静房间里的一道声音开始，再到你无法拒收的账单，最后到独自做出的投票。

normal.en: Con- is with and sci- is know, so conscience is knowing with yourself.
normal.cn: con- 是与，sci- 是知道，conscience 就是与自己一同知道。

normal.en: A clear conscience sleeps well; a guilty one keeps the light on.
normal.cn: 问心无愧的人睡得香，心虚的人一直开着灯。

normal.en: The judge wears no robe and sits inside your chest.
normal.cn: 这位法官不穿法袍，就坐在你胸口里面。

normal.en: Doing right when nobody watches is the whole test.
normal.cn: 没人看着时仍做对的事，这就是全部的考验。

normal.en: A matter of conscience is one you cannot hand to someone else.
normal.cn: 良心问题，是你没法转交给别人的问题。

abstract.en: Picture a small lamp still burning in an empty room.
abstract.cn: 想象空房间里一盏还亮着的小灯。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing back a coin across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一枚硬币推回柜台。

abstract.en: Picture a mark made on a paper while no one looks.
abstract.cn: 想象无人旁观时在纸上画下的一个记号。

examples.en: His conscience would not let him lie.
examples.cn: 他的良心不容他撒谎。

examples.en: She has a clear conscience about the decision.
examples.cn: 她对这个决定问心无愧。

examples.en: The question troubled his conscience for years.
examples.cn: 这个问题让他的良心不安了好多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conscience 记成 con（与自己一起）加 sci（知道）：心里那个知道你所有事的小声音，就是良心。

root: 源自拉丁语 conscientia（com 与 + scire 知道），本义是与自己共知，后指内心善恶的判断力与内疚感。

sensesIntro.en: From the inward judge, to the guilt it leaves behind, and finally to a moral stand taken in public.
sensesIntro.cn: 从内心的审判者，到它留下的内疚，最后到公开场合下的道义立场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quiet voice in an empty room that knows what you did.
core.cn: 核心意象：空房间里一道安静的声音，知道你都做过什么。

branches.en: The core sense is the ability to judge your own acts.
branches.cn: 核心义项是评判自身行为的能力。

branches.en: When the judgement goes against you, it becomes guilt.
branches.cn: 当判断对你不利时，它就变成内疚。

branches.en: The same sense can guide a public stand on a hard question.
branches.cn: 同一种感受也能指引人在难题上公开表态。

branches.en: The judge and the pain are one system working inside a person.
branches.cn: 审判者与痛苦，是同一套在人心内运作的系统。

branches.en: Guilt is private, while a matter of conscience can be public.
branches.cn: 内疚是私下的，而良心问题可以是公开的。

intro.en: Conscience is built on Latin com-, with, plus scire, to know.
intro.cn: conscience 由拉丁语 com-（与）与 scire（知道）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin know base sci- also appears in conscious, science and omniscient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的知道词基 sci- 也出现在 conscious、science 与 omniscient 中。

items.meaning: knowledge of right and wrong within oneself

items.example: She was conscious of the danger.

items.meaning: careful to do what is right
items.exampleCN: 她是个认真负责的员工。

items.meaningCN: 失去知觉的或未察觉的
items.example: He was unconscious for a minute.
items.exampleCN: 他有一分钟失去了知觉。

items.meaning: below the level of full awareness
items.example: A subconscious fear held him back.
items.exampleCN: 一种潜藏的恐惧拖住了他。
这个叙述者听起来无所不知。

definition_zh: 不受控制的；不加克制的；未受管制的；无节制的
definition_en: not kept within limits by anyone or anything
core_image: 缰绳脱了手，马车顺着坡自己往下冲
scene: 山路上，送货的三轮车刹车失灵，车主只能大声让路人躲开。 Uncontrolled spending left the family without savings.
sceneCN: 这里 uncontrolled 是「不受控制的」（第 1 个义项：失去约束）；句意为无节制的开销让这家人没有存款。脱手的缰绳让车自己冲下坡，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：不受控制的；失控的
形容词：未受管制的；未经检查的

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀的原词，义为「控制；管理」
过去分词作形容词，义为「受控制的」
动词加 -er 构成，义为「控制者；控制器」

senses.title: Not kept in check
senses.definition: of a feeling or force, running on without restraint
senses.definitionCN: 就情绪或力量而言，不受约束地继续下去
senses.example: His uncontrolled temper frightened the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他那股不加克制的脾气让全班害怕。
senses.why: Control comes from a medieval roll kept for checking accounts, so un- means the roll is no longer being checked.
senses.whyCN: control 源自中世纪用于核对账目的卷册，un- 意味着这本卷册不再被核对。

senses.title: Not regulated by authority
senses.definition: not supervised or limited by an official body
senses.definitionCN: 没有官方机构的监督或限制
senses.example: Uncontrolled dumping polluted the river.
senses.exampleCN: 不受管制的倾倒污染了这条河。
senses.why: Where no ledger is kept, nothing is checked, and a rule that is not checked is no rule.
senses.whyCN: 没有账簿的地方就无人核对，而不被核对的规则等于没有规则。

senses.title: Growing or spreading without limit
senses.definition: increasing with no limit or plan
senses.definitionCN: 没有限度或计划地增加
senses.example: The city faces uncontrolled building on its edges.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市面临边缘地带无节制的建设。
senses.why: Growth that no one measures simply keeps adding itself, brick after brick.
senses.whyCN: 无人度量的增长只会一块砖接一块砖地自己加上去。

senses.title: Not restrained in the body
senses.definition: of movement, shaking, or crying that the body cannot stop
senses.definitionCN: 指抖动、哭泣等身体动作止不下来
senses.example: Uncontrolled shivering followed the fever.
senses.exampleCN: 发烧之后接着是不停的发抖。
senses.why: When the reins are gone, the body no longer obeys the will.
senses.whyCN: 缰绳一断，身体就不再听意志的指挥。

senses.title: Lacking a comparison group in research
senses.definition: of a trial, carried out without a comparison group to check results
senses.definitionCN: 指试验没有设对照组来核对结果
senses.example: An uncontrolled trial cannot prove the drug works.
senses.exampleCN: 未设对照组的试验无法证明这种药有效。
senses.why: In science control means the standard kept for comparison, so uncontrolled means no such standard exists.
senses.whyCN: 科学里 control 指用于比较的标准样本，uncontrolled 就是没有这个标准。

intro.en: The word is the past participle of control with a negative prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词是 control 的过去分词加否定前缀。

items.en: Contrarotulus is a roll kept against a duplicate roll for checking accounts.
items.cn: contrarotulus 是与另一本副本卷册并置、用于核对账目的卷册。

items.en: Old French contrerolle carries the account-checking sense of the word.
items.cn: 古法语 contrerolle 保留了核对账目之义。

items.en: English control first means to check accounts, then to direct anything.
items.cn: 英语 control 先指核对账目，后指对任何事物的支配。

items.en: Uncontrolled appears in the eighteenth century for what escapes checking.
items.cn: uncontrolled 在十八世纪出现，指逃出核对的东西。

items.en: Science adopts controlled and uncontrolled for trials in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪，科学界用 controlled 与 uncontrolled 称呼试验。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the control family, and the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of unrestrained force.
note.cn: 形近组展示 control 词族，近义组汇集表示约束失效的形容词。

kept within limits

normalIntro.en: Control began as a copy ledger kept for checking, and losing it means losing the check.
normalIntro.cn: control 最初是一本用来核对的副本账簿，丢了它就丢了核对。

normal.en: Contra- means against and rotulus is a roll, so control is a check roll held beside the account.
normal.cn: contra- 意为相对，rotulus 是卷册，control 就是放在账册旁的核对卷。

normal.en: The controlled object of a verb and the controlled style of writing both come from that check.
normal.cn: 动词的宾语叫 object，写作的自制叫 controlled，都出自这层核对。

normal.en: Uncontrolled laughter and uncontrolled growth share the lack of a check.
normal.cn: uncontrolled laughter 与 uncontrolled growth 共享「缺少核对」这一层。

normal.en: Controlled experiment and uncontrolled trial are the two poles in research.
normal.cn: controlled experiment 与 uncontrolled trial 是研究里的两极。

normal.en: English says more uncontrolled, not uncontrolleder.
normal.cn: 英语说 more uncontrolled，不说 uncontrolleder。

abstract.en: Feel reins slip out of your fingers on a slope.
abstract.cn: 感觉缰绳在坡上从指间滑脱。

abstract.en: Watch a garden grow over its fence in one summer.
abstract.cn: 看一座花园在一个夏天里长过围栏。

abstract.en: Then see a ledger left open with no one checking it.
abstract.cn: 再看一本摊开无人核对的账册。

examples.en: Uncontrolled fires have destroyed large areas of forest.
examples.cn: 失控的大火毁掉了大片森林。

examples.en: Her uncontrolled laughter filled the whole corridor.
examples.cn: 她止不住的笑声传遍了整条走廊。

examples.en: The drug was tested in an uncontrolled trial only.
examples.cn: 这种药只在未设对照组的试验中测试过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安控球得」——球一旦安不住，控不住就得看着它滚下坡。

root: un-（否定前缀）+ controlled（control 加 -ed；control 源自中世纪拉丁语 contrarotulus「核对卷册」，由 contra-「相对」+ rotulus「卷」构成）

sensesIntro.en: Whatever escapes a check is uncontrolled: a temper, a market, a fire, a shaking body, or a trial without a comparison group.
sensesIntro.cn: 任何逃出核对的东西都是 uncontrolled：脾气、市场、火、发抖的身体，或没有对照组的试验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reins slipping free on a downhill road.
core.cn: 核心意象：下坡路上脱了手的缰绳。

branches.en: The feeling branch: anger and laughter that will not stop.
branches.cn: 情绪分支：止不住的怒气与笑声。

branches.en: The authority branch: dumping and building no one supervises.
branches.cn: 权力分支：无人监管的倾倒与建设。

branches.en: The growth branch: expansion with no plan.
branches.cn: 增长分支：没有计划的扩张。

branches.en: The body branch: shivering the will cannot stop.
branches.cn: 身体分支：意志止不住的颤抖。

branches.en: The research branch, where control means a comparison group.
branches.cn: 研究分支：这里的 control 指对照组。

intro.en: A negation prefix on a participle of checking and directing.
intro.cn: 否定前缀盖在表示核对与支配的分词上。

latinIntro.en: The roll image in contrarotulus survives in the modern word.
latinIntro.cn: contrarotulus 里那卷账簿的意象一直留在现代词中。

items.example: Contra- sits at the front of control.
items.exampleCN: contra- 位于 control 词首。

items.example: The roll was the account book.

definition_zh: 褪色；逐渐消失；减弱；衰退
definition_en: to lose colour or brightness; to become gradually weaker or quieter until it disappears; to decline in strength or importance
core_image: 阳光把布料的颜色一点点晒淡，直到几乎看不见
scene: 窗帘被太阳晒得褪色了。 The curtains faded in the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 fade 是「褪色」（第 1 个义项）；句意：窗帘被太阳晒得褪色了。

senses.title: To lose colour
senses.definition: to lose colour or brightness over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间失去颜色或光泽
senses.example: The curtains faded in the strong sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘在强烈的阳光下褪色了。
senses.why: The core sense is colour slowly leaving a surface.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是颜色慢慢从表面退去。

senses.title: To become weaker
senses.definition: to become gradually weaker, quieter, or less clear until it disappears
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐变弱、变轻或变模糊直至消失
senses.example: The music faded as the train left.
senses.exampleCN: 火车开走时音乐声渐渐消失。
senses.why: Sound and light fade in the same soft way as colour.
senses.whyCN: 声音与光线像颜色一样柔和地消退。

senses.title: To decline
senses.definition: to lose strength, importance, or energy
senses.definitionCN: 失去力量、重要性或活力
senses.example: His hopes of winning faded over the season.
senses.exampleCN: 他夺冠的希望随着赛季推进逐渐破灭。
senses.why: The image of fading colour extends to abstract strength.
senses.whyCN: 褪色的意象延伸到抽象的力量。

intro.en: Fade comes from Old French fade, pale, probably from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: fade 来自古法语 fade（苍白的），可能源于日耳曼词根。

items.en: Fade means pale or dull.
items.cn: fade 意为苍白的、暗淡的。

items.en: The verb means to lose colour.
items.cn: 中古英语中该动词意为失去颜色。

items.en: Fade also describes light growing weak.
items.cn: 十六世纪 fade 也描述光线变弱。

items.en: Fade describes sounds dying away.
items.cn: 十九世纪 fade 描述声音渐逝。

items.en: Fade in and fade out name film transitions.
items.cn: 现代英语用 fade in 与 fade out 指影视转场。

note.en: Fade means to grow faint; fate is what is destined to happen.
note.cn: fade 是逐渐变淡，fate 则是命运。

entries.definition: the power that decides events
not genuine
the front of the head
to become or make less bright
to become smaller or weaker
to disappear completely

normalIntro.en: Fade is the slow loss of colour, sound, or strength.
normalIntro.cn: fade 是颜色、声音或力量的缓慢流失。

normal.en: The old photographs have faded.
normal.cn: 这些旧照片已经褪色了。

normal.en: Her voice faded into silence.
normal.cn: 她的声音渐渐归于寂静。

normal.en: The memory of that day faded.
normal.cn: 那天的记忆渐渐淡去。

normal.en: The music faded out at the end.
normal.cn: 音乐在结尾处淡出。

normal.en: His enthusiasm faded after a few weeks.
normal.cn: 几周后他的热情消退了。

abstract.en: Picture a bright shirt left for years in the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一件鲜艳衬衫在阳光下晒了多年。

abstract.en: Imagine a sound walking slowly out of hearing.
abstract.cn: 想象声音慢慢走出听觉范围。

abstract.en: Think of a hope growing thinner like mist.
abstract.cn: 把希望想成越来越薄的雾。

examples.en: The blue paint had faded to grey.
examples.cn: 蓝色油漆已经褪成了灰色。

examples.en: The applause faded as the curtain fell.
examples.cn: 幕布落下时掌声渐渐平息。

examples.en: Her anger faded when she heard the truth.
examples.cn: 她听到真相后怒意消退了。

dict_mnemonic.text: fade 原意是「苍白、暗淡」，颜色、声音、记忆由浓转淡的过程都是 fade。

root: fade 来自古法语 fade（苍白的、暗淡的），可能源于日耳曼词根，本义与「失去鲜明」有关。

sensesIntro.en: Fade means to lose colour, to grow weaker, or to decline.
sensesIntro.cn: fade 意为褪色、逐渐变弱或衰退。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: colour and sound slowly thinning away.
core.cn: 核心意象：颜色与声音慢慢变淡。

branches.en: The base sense is losing colour.
branches.cn: 基础义是失去颜色。

branches.en: Light and sound grow weak in the same way.
branches.cn: 光线与声音以同样方式变弱。

branches.en: Abstract strength also declines.
branches.cn: 抽象的力量同样会衰退。

branches.en: Both are gradual losses of intensity.
branches.cn: 两者都是强度的逐渐流失。

branches.en: What fades may vanish or simply weaken.
branches.cn: 消退之物可能消失，也可能只是变弱。

intro.en: Fade is a short verb that builds adjectives and phrasal verbs.
intro.cn: fade 是一个短动词，能构成形容词与短语动词。

latinIntro.en: Fade has no Latin root; its history is French and Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: fade 没有拉丁词根，其历史属于法语与日耳曼语。

items.example: The fading light warned us to go home.
items.exampleCN: 渐暗的光线提醒我们该回家了。

items.example: She kept an unfading memory of him.
items.exampleCN: 她对他保持着不褪色的记忆。

definition_zh: 解开；打开；取消；撤销；毁掉（某人的前途）
definition_en: to reverse something done, such as a knot, a change, or a plan
core_image: 把系紧的结一根根抽开，布又摊平了
scene: 缝纫课上，学员发现领子缝反了，只好一针针拆开再来。 She had to undo three hours of work.
sceneCN: 这里 undo 是「解开、拆开」（第 1 个义项：把已做的东西还原）；句意为她不得不把三个小时的活全部拆掉。把系紧的结抽开让布摊平，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 过去分词作形容词，义为「未做完的；毁了的」
动词加 -ing 构成名词，义为「毁灭；败因」
动词加 -able 构成形容词，义为「可撤销的」

senses.title: To open what is fastened
senses.definition: to unfasten a button, a knot, or a zip
senses.definitionCN: 把纽扣、绳结或拉链松开
senses.example: He undid the top button of his collar.
senses.exampleCN: 他解开了衣领上那颗扣子。
senses.why: The verb is un- plus do, so it undoes the doing of a fastening.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 un- 加 do，把「系上」这个动作反过来做。

senses.title: To cancel the effect of something
senses.definition: to remove the harm caused by an earlier action
senses.definitionCN: 消除先前行为造成的损害
senses.example: One apology cannot undo years of neglect.
senses.exampleCN: 一句道歉消不掉多年的冷淡。
senses.why: If the effect is a knot, the reversal is an untying, and the same picture serves harm.
senses.whyCN: 若效果是一个结，反转就是解开它，同一个画面也能用来化解伤害。

senses.title: To reverse a step on a computer
senses.definition: to cancel the last command or editing step
senses.definitionCN: 取消上一条指令或编辑步骤
senses.example: Press this key to undo the change.
senses.exampleCN: 按这个键撤销刚才的修改。
senses.why: A command is a knot tied in the machine, and undo pulls the thread back out.
senses.whyCN: 一条指令是系在机器里的结，undo 就是把它抽回去。

senses.title: To bring ruin to a person
senses.definition: to cause someone’s ruin or failure
senses.definitionCN: 使某人身败名裂或事业失败
senses.example: Drink finally undid him.
senses.exampleCN: 酒最终毁了他。
senses.why: To undo a person is to take apart what was built, thread by thread.
senses.whyCN: 毁掉一个人，就是把他建起来的东西一根线一根线拆掉。

senses.title: To come loose by itself
senses.definition: of something fastened, to work loose, or of a plan, to collapse
senses.definitionCN: 指系好的东西自行松开，或计划崩解
senses.example: The whole plan came undone in a week.
senses.exampleCN: 整个计划一周之内就崩了。
senses.why: When the fastening gives way on its own, the word turns intransitive and the thing falls apart.
senses.whyCN: 系紧的东西自己松开时，这个词转为不及物，那东西就此散掉。

intro.en: The word is the English prefix un- set against the oldest English verb.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语前缀 un- 加在最古老的英语动词 do 之前。

items.en: The prefix un- is used to reverse a verb, and dōn means to do or to make.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 用于反转动词，dōn 意为做、作成。

items.en: Undōn is recorded in the sense of opening or unfastening.
items.cn: undōn 已有「打开、解开」之义的记录。

items.en: Middle English undoon keeps that sense and adds the sense of ruin.
items.cn: 中古英语 undoon 保留该义，并添出「毁坏」之义。

items.en: The computing sense of reversing a command arrives in the late twentieth century.
items.cn: 撤销计算机指令的义项在二十世纪后期出现。

items.en: The irregular past forms undid and undone survive intact.
items.cn: 不规则过去式 undid 与过去分词 undone 完整保存至今。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers un- verbs that reverse an action, and the near-meaning group collects verbs of cancelling.
note.cn: 形近组汇集表反向的 un- 动词，近义组汇集表示取消的动词。

normalIntro.en: Un- reverses, and do is the plainest verb, so undo is the plainest reversal.
normalIntro.cn: un- 表反转，do 是最朴素的动词，undo 就是最朴素的反转。

normal.en: The verb is irregular: undo today, undid yesterday, undone in the past participle.
normal.cn: 这个词不规则：现在 undo，过去 undid，过去分词 undone。

normal.en: Undo a button is the everyday sense at a collar.
normal.cn: undo a button 是衣领上最日常的用法。

normal.en: Press undo when a change goes wrong on a screen.
normal.cn: 屏幕上改错了就按 undo。

normal.en: Come undone means something came apart, from a hem to a plan.
normal.cn: come undone 指东西散了，从衣边到计划都行。

normal.en: Undoing as a noun is the thing that ruins a person.
normal.cn: 名词 undoing 指毁掉一个人的那个东西。

abstract.en: Take a tight knot and pull one thread at a time.
abstract.cn: 拿一个紧结，一次抽一根线。

abstract.en: Watch the cloth flatten again as the knot gives way.
abstract.cn: 看结散开后布重新摊平。

abstract.en: Then see a whole plan come loose the same way.
abstract.cn: 再看整个计划以同样方式松散。

examples.en: She undid the knot with her teeth.
examples.cn: 她用牙把那个结咬开了。

examples.en: No amount of money could undo the damage.
examples.cn: 再多的钱也无法消除那场损害。

examples.en: The scandal undid a career of thirty years.
examples.cn: 这场丑闻毁掉了三十年的职业生涯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安堵」——心一安堵，就把缠着的结全解开了。

root: un-（反向前缀）+ do（古英语 dōn「做」）；undōn 原指解开、打开，过去式 undid，过去分词 undone

sensesIntro.en: Every sense reverses a fastening or a building up, whether a button, a harm, a command, a career, or a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都在反转一次系紧或一次建立：纽扣、伤害、指令、事业或计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knot pulled apart until the cloth lies flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：结被抽开，布重新摊平。

branches.en: The hands branch: buttons, knots, and zips.
branches.cn: 手上分支：纽扣、绳结与拉链。

branches.en: The repair branch: harm and mistakes put right.
branches.cn: 修复分支：纠正伤害与错误。

branches.en: The digital branch: one step back on a screen.
branches.cn: 数字分支：屏幕上退一步。

branches.en: The ruin branch: a person or a plan taken apart.
branches.cn: 毁坏分支：被拆散的人或计划。

branches.en: The plain sense met at a shirt collar.
branches.cn: 衬衫领口最常见的朴素义。

intro.en: A reversing prefix on the simplest of English verbs.
intro.cn: 反向前缀加在英语最简单的动词上。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁同源词一栏留空。

definition_zh: 庄严的；隆重的；严肃的；郑重其事的
definition_en: formal and serious in a religious or public setting, not cheerful, or made as a serious promise
core_image: 安静的礼堂里人们肃立不语
scene: 婚礼是庄严的场合。 The wedding was a solemn occasion.
sceneCN: 这里 solemn 是「庄严的；隆重的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：婚礼是庄严的场合。

senses.title: Formal and grand
senses.definition: formal and serious in a public or religious ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 在公共或宗教仪式中正式而严肃的
senses.example: The wedding was a solemn occasion.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼是一个庄严的场合。
senses.why: This is the ceremonial sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是仪式性的义项。

senses.title: Serious in manner
senses.definition: serious and not cheerful in expression or manner
senses.definitionCN: 表情或举止严肃、不轻松的
senses.example: He listened with a solemn face.
senses.exampleCN: 他板着严肃的面孔听。
senses.why: The word describes a person's manner.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述一个人的举止。

senses.title: Made as a vow
senses.definition: made as a serious and binding promise
senses.definitionCN: 作为严肃而有约束力的承诺作出的
senses.example: She made a solemn promise to return.
senses.exampleCN: 她郑重承诺会回来。
senses.why: A promise borrows the weight of ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 承诺借用了仪式的分量。

intro.en: Solemn comes from Latin sollemnis, meaning fixed or ceremonial.
intro.cn: solemn 来自拉丁语 sollemnis，意为固定的或仪式的。

items.en: Sollemnis meant yearly, fixed, or ceremonial.
items.cn: sollemnis 意为每年的、固定的或仪式的。

items.en: Solemne kept the sense of religious formality.
items.cn: solemne 保留了宗教仪式的正式含义。

items.en: The word entered English as solemn.
items.cn: 这个词以 solemn 进入英语。

items.en: It widened to any serious public event.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何严肃的公共活动。

items.en: It also described a serious promise or manner.
items.cn: 它也形容严肃的承诺或举止。

note.en: Solemn is compared with look-alike words and words for serious manner.
note.cn: 把 solemn 与形近词以及表示严肃举止的词作比较。

entries.definition: a tall stone post or a vertical section
making no sound
only or single
not joking or light
very serious and worrying
following official rules or ceremony

normalIntro.en: Solemn marks an occasion heavy with meaning and quiet.
normalIntro.cn: solemn 标记一个意义沉重、安静无声的场合。

normal.en: The wedding was a solemn occasion.
normal.cn: 婚礼是一个庄严的场合。

normal.en: He listened with a solemn face.
normal.cn: 他板着严肃的面孔听。

normal.en: She made a solemn promise to return.
normal.cn: 她郑重承诺会回来。

normal.en: A solemn silence filled the hall.
normal.cn: 肃穆的寂静充满大厅。

normal.en: Solemn music began as they entered.
normal.cn: 他们入场时响起了庄严的音乐。

abstract.en: Some moments ask us to be still and mean it.
abstract.cn: 有些时刻要求我们安静下来，并且真心如此。

abstract.en: A promise is heavier when it is spoken slowly.
abstract.cn: 慢慢说出的承诺更沉重。

abstract.en: Ceremony gives shape to feelings too large for words.
abstract.cn: 仪式给无法言说的情感以形状。

examples.en: The wedding was a solemn occasion.
examples.cn: 婚礼是一个庄严的场合。

examples.en: He listened with a solemn face.
examples.cn: 他板着严肃的面孔听。

examples.en: She made a solemn promise to return.
examples.cn: 她郑重承诺会回来。

dict_mnemonic.text: solemn 与 column 形近；a solemn promise 是「郑重承诺」，a solemn occasion 是「庄严场合」。

root: 拉丁语 sollemnis（每年举行的、固定的、仪式的），经古法语 solemne 进入英语，核心义「庄重有仪式感的」。

sensesIntro.en: Solemn means formal and grand, serious in manner, or made as a binding promise.
sensesIntro.cn: solemn 意为庄严隆重的、举止严肃的，或作为有约束力承诺的。

core.en: A moment made heavy by meaning.
core.cn: 因意义而变得沉重的时刻。

branches.en: Guests stand for a wedding.
branches.cn: 宾客在婚礼上肃立。

branches.en: A face holds back a smile.
branches.cn: 一张脸忍住不笑。

branches.en: Words are spoken as a vow.
branches.cn: 话语作为誓言说出。

branches.en: Ceremony and promise borrow each other's weight.
branches.cn: 仪式与承诺互相借来分量。

branches.en: A serious face makes a promise believable.
branches.cn: 严肃的面孔让承诺可信。

intro.en: Solemn builds words for ceremony, seriousness, and vows.
intro.cn: solemn 构成表示仪式、严肃和誓言的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source sollemnis meant ceremonial or yearly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源 sollemnis 意为仪式的或每年的。

items.example: The hall fell solemn and still.
The room was full of solemnity.
The memorial was a solemn occasion.
items.exampleCN: 纪念仪式是一个庄严场合。

items.example: She wore a solemn face all morning.
items.exampleCN: 她整个上午都板着严肃的面孔。

items.example: A solemn silence followed the news.
items.exampleCN: 消息传来后是一片肃穆的寂静。

latinEntries.example: Sollemnis is the Latin source of solemn.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sollemnis 是 solemn 的拉丁语来源。

definition_zh: 代词
definition_en: a word such as he, she, it or they that is used in place of a noun or a noun phrase
core_image: 一个人指着空椅子说「他」，椅子上没有人，那个名字已被一个短词顶替
scene: 介绍新同事时，老员工不愿反复念那个长名字，只用「他」来指，大家也都听得懂。 The pronoun saved everyone from repeating the long name in every sentence.
sceneCN: 这里表示「代词」（第 1 个义项：用来代替名词或名词短语的词）；句意为代词让大家不必在每句话里重复那个长名字。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 pronomin- 加 -al 构成，义为「代词的；起代词作用的」
由 pronominal 加 -ly 构成，义为「以代词的方式」

senses.title: A word that stands in for a noun
senses.definition: a word used instead of a noun or noun phrase, so that the same name does not have to be repeated
senses.definitionCN: 用来代替名词或名词短语的词，免得同一个名字反复出现
senses.example: In the sentence she wrote it, both she and it are pronouns.
senses.exampleCN: 在 she wrote it 这句话里，she 与 it 都是代词。
senses.why: Latin pro- means for or instead of and nomen means name, so the word is literally a stand-in for a name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pro- 意为「代替、为了」，nomen 意为「名字」，所以这个词字面上就是「名字的替身」。

senses.title: A pronoun marking who speaks, is spoken to, or is spoken about
senses.definition: a pronoun that points to the speaker, the listener, or a third person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 指说话人、听话人，或第三方的人与物的代词
senses.example: I, you, he, she, we and they are personal pronouns.
senses.exampleCN: I、you、he、she、we、they 都是人称代词。
senses.why: Grammarians sorted the class by the three roles of a conversation, so the pronouns that mark those roles received a name of their own.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家按对话的三方角色给这一类词再分类，标出这些角色的代词便单独有了名称。

senses.title: A pronoun that introduces a clause and links it to a noun
senses.definition: a pronoun such as who, which or that that opens a subordinate clause and connects it to the noun before it
senses.definitionCN: 像 who、which、that 这样引出从句并把它接到前面名词上的代词
senses.example: In the phrase the man who called, who is a relative pronoun.
senses.exampleCN: 在 the man who called 这个短语里，who 是关系代词。
senses.why: A relative pronoun still stands for the noun in front of it, yet at the same moment it opens a clause, so one short word does two jobs.
senses.whyCN: 关系代词仍然代替它前面的名词，同时又引出一个从句，于是一个短词兼做两件事。

senses.title: A pronoun that shows possession without the noun
senses.definition: a pronoun such as mine, yours or theirs that carries the idea of ownership while the noun is left out
senses.definitionCN: 像 mine、yours、theirs 这样带着归属含义、却把名词省去的代词
senses.example: Mine and theirs are possessive pronouns because each replaces a whole noun phrase.
senses.exampleCN: mine 与 theirs 是物主代词，因为它们各自代替了一整个名词短语。
senses.why: The possessive form keeps the ownership but drops the owned thing, which is exactly the substituting work a pronoun does.
senses.whyCN: 物主形式保留了归属，却省掉了被归属的东西，这正是代词「顶替」的本职。

intro.en: Pronoun is a Latin translation of a Greek grammar term: pro- for instead of, nomen for name. It names a word that occupies the place a name would take.
intro.cn: pronoun 是对一个希腊语法术语的拉丁翻译：pro- 意为代替，nomen 意为名字。它指的就是占据名字位置的词。

items.en: Nomen meant name, and it also supplied noun and a whole family of words about naming.
items.cn: nomen 意为名字，也是 noun 以及一整族与命名有关的词的来源。

items.en: Greek grammarians called the class antonymia, built from anti, instead of, and onoma, name.
items.cn: 希腊语法学家把这一类词称作 antonymia，由 anti（代替）与 onoma（名字）构成。

items.en: Latin teachers translated the Greek term piece by piece, producing pronomen, literally a word standing for a name.
items.cn: 拉丁语教师把这个希腊术语逐块翻译，造出 pronomen，字面就是「代替名字的词」。

items.en: Old French pronom carried the grammar label into English use, and the spelling later settled as pronoun.
items.cn: 古法语 pronom 把这个语法标签带进英语，拼写后来固定为 pronoun。

items.en: English keeps pronoun as the general label and names each subclass by the work it does in the sentence.
items.cn: 现代英语把 pronoun 保留为总称，再按各小类在句中的功能分别命名。

note.en: The first group collects same-root relatives plus two words that merely look alike and must not be confused; the second group collects the other word classes a pronoun is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组收同源近亲，外加两个只是长得像、必须分清的词；第二组收与代词常被放在一起比较的其他词类。

entries.definition: A word for a person, place or thing; it shares the Latin name-word but does the naming itself.
entries.definitionCN: 表示人、地或物的词；与本词共用拉丁「名字」一词，但它自己就是命名的那一方。

entries.definition: Relating to a pronoun, or behaving like one in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 与代词有关的，或在句中起代词作用的。

entries.definition: To say a word aloud; only the spelling is close, the origin is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 把词读出声；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The way a word is spoken; it looks like this word but has nothing to do with grammar, only the spelling is close and the origin is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 词的读法；它看起来像这个词，却与语法无关，只是拼写相近、词源不同。

entries.definition: A word for an action or a state, another word class.
entries.definitionCN: 表示动作或状态的词，属于另一词类。

entries.definition: A word that describes or limits a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰或限定名词的词；形容词。

entries.definition: A word that modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰动词、形容词或另一副词的词。

entries.definition: A word such as the or this placed before a noun to limit it.
entries.definitionCN: 像 the 或 this 那样放在名词前起限定作用的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a literal translation of a Greek grammar term, which is why its two halves still say exactly what it does: in place of a name.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是对一个希腊语法术语的逐字翻译，所以它的两半至今仍直接说出它的功能：站在名字的位置上。

normal.en: Pro- in Latin means for or instead of, and nomen means name, so pronomen is a word taking the place of a name.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pro- 意为「代替、为了」，nomen 意为名字，所以 pronomen 就是替名字站位的词。

normal.en: Greek grammarians said anti plus onoma; Latin teachers translated both halves, which is why the English word is so transparent.
normal.cn: 希腊语法学家说 anti 加 onoma；拉丁语教师把两半都译了出来，所以英语这个词一眼就能看懂。

normal.en: Personal pronouns divide by who is speaking, so one class is seen from three positions in the conversation.
normal.cn: 人称代词按「谁在说」来分，于是同一个词类从对话的三个位置来看。

normal.en: A relative pronoun replaces a noun and joins a clause at the same time, which is how who can do the work of two words.
normal.cn: 关系代词既代替名词又连接从句，所以 who 能做一个两词才能做的活。

normal.en: A possessive pronoun keeps the ownership but drops the noun, so mine stands for my something without naming it.
normal.cn: 物主代词保留归属、省掉名词，所以 mine 代替 my 加某物，却不必说出那是什么。

abstract.en: A pronoun is economy in grammar: it lets a language avoid saying the same name twice.
abstract.cn: 代词是语法里的节省：它让语言不必把同一个名字说两遍。

abstract.en: Every pronoun leans on something said earlier, so the class is a reminder that words can point instead of name.
abstract.cn: 每个代词都倚靠前面说过的东西，所以这个词类提醒人：词可以指，而不必命名。

abstract.en: Because a pronoun can change referent with a glance or a gesture, grammar and pointing share one small word.
abstract.cn: 由于一个眼神或手势就能改变代词的所指，语法与指点动作共用一个小词。

examples.en: Every pronoun in the paragraph refers back to the scientist.
examples.cn: 这一段里的每个代词都回指那位科学家。

examples.en: Use a pronoun instead of the full name when the meaning is clear.
examples.cn: 意思清楚时用代词代替全名。

examples.en: The pronoun they can now refer to a single person.
examples.cn: 代词 they 现在也能指单个人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若诺恩」——把长名字折成一个短音，像把名字缩成影子；记住 pronoun 是代词。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（代替、为了）+ nomen（名字）→ pronomen（代替名字的词）；一般认为这是拉丁语法学家对希腊语 anti 加 onoma 的逐字翻译，经古法语 pronom 进入英语。注意它与 pronunciation（发音）只是拼写相近，来源与意义都不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a word standing where a name would stand; the personal, relative and possessive subclasses each show one kind of work that stand-in can do.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「站在名字位置上的词」；人称、关系、物主等小类，各自展示这个替身能做的一种活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointing at an empty chair while a short word does the work of a long name.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指着空椅子，一个短词顶替了那个长名字。

branches.en: a long name folded into one short word
branches.cn: 长长的名字被折成一个短词

branches.en: three people in a conversation, each with a pronoun
branches.cn: 对话中的三方各有自己的代词

branches.en: a clause joined to a noun by a single word
branches.cn: 一个词把从句接到名词上

branches.en: ownership kept while the object is left out
branches.cn: 归属还在，被归属的东西却省去了

branches.en: the same stand-in doing different jobs
branches.cn: 同一个替身做着不同的活

intro.en: A Latin prefix of substitution, the Latin word for name, and the endings that make the adjective and the adverb hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示代替的拉丁前缀、拉丁语的「名字」，以及造出形容词与副词的词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Pronomen and nomen are the reliable Latin cognates; the Greek term behind them is usually cited as the model that Latin teachers translated.
latinIntro.cn: pronomen 与 nomen 是可靠的同源词；它们背后的希腊术语，一般认为就是拉丁语教师所模仿翻译的原型。

definition_zh: 使文明；教化；使有教养
definition_en: to bring a society to a more developed way of life, or to make someone behave in a more polite and educated way
core_image: 荒地上同时立起学校、道路与法庭
scene: 老师带学生看老照片，照片里是从前的村路。 Missionaries tried to civilize the remote islands.
sceneCN: 这里 civilize 指「使文明」（第 1 个义项：把一个社会带向更发达的生活方式）；句意是传教士试图使那些偏远岛屿文明起来。

senses.title: To develop a society
senses.definition: to bring a society to a more advanced stage with cities, writing and law
senses.definitionCN: 把一个社会带向有城市、文字与法律的更发达阶段
senses.example: Trade routes helped civilize the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 商路帮助沿海地区走向文明。
senses.why: The verb names the act of pushing a group towards the civilized state.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词指推动一个群体走向文明状态的行为。

senses.title: To teach good manners
senses.definition: to make a person or group behave with polite and educated habits
senses.definitionCN: 使人或群体养成礼貌而有教养的习惯
senses.example: Years abroad had civilized his table manners.
senses.exampleCN: 多年在外的经历让他的餐桌礼仪变得文雅。
senses.why: Good manners were treated as a small private version of the same process.
senses.whyCN: 良好举止被视为同一过程在私人层面的小版本。

intro.en: The verb is the action behind civilization, built on the Latin word for a citizen.
intro.cn: 这个动词是文明背后的动作，建立在拉丁语表示公民的词上。

items.en: Civilis meant of a citizen.
items.cn: civilis 意为公民的。

items.en: Civiliser meant to make civil or fit for society.
items.cn: civiliser 意为使变得文明或适合社会。

items.en: English took the verb as civilize and kept the French sense.
items.cn: 英语以 civilize 借入这个动词，保留了法语的含义。

items.en: Writers used it for nations as well as for manners.
items.cn: 作家们既用它说民族，也用它说举止。

items.en: The word now often carries a critical tone about outside interference.
items.cn: 这个词如今常带批评外部干预的口气。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the civil family, while the meaning group names acts of improving people.
note.cn: 形近组列出 civil 家族，近义组列出使人变好的各种动作。

entries.definition: polite, or relating to citizens
entries.definitionCN: 有礼的，或与公民有关的

entries.definition: a person who is not in the armed forces
polite behaviour or a polite remark
to teach someone over a long period
to improve something by small changes
entries.definitionCN: 通过细微改变来改善某物

entries.definition: to give someone knowledge and understanding

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the citizen root, the -ize ending and the contrast between nations and manners.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用公民词根、-ize 后缀以及民族与举止的对比。

normal.en: Civilize is civil plus -ize, so it means to make something civil.
normal.cn: civilize 是 civil 加 -ize，所以意思是使某物变得文明。

normal.en: The verb is transitive: someone always civilizes someone else.
normal.cn: 这个动词是及物的：总是一方教化另一方。

normal.en: Nations can be civilized, and so can table manners.
normal.cn: 民族可以被开化，餐桌礼仪也可以变得文雅。

normal.en: The -ize ending marks an action, while -ization marks the resulting process or state.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ize 表示动作，-ization 表示由此形成的过程或状态。

normal.en: Modern writers often avoid the verb because it sounds one-sided.
normal.cn: 现代作家常避开这个动词，因为它听起来居高临下。

abstract.en: Picture a road and a school appearing together on an empty plain.
abstract.cn: 想象空旷平原上同时出现一条路和一所学校。

abstract.en: Picture a visitor correcting a child's grip on a fork.
abstract.cn: 想象一位客人纠正孩子拿叉子的手势。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the shaded area slowly spreads inland.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上着色区域慢慢向内陆扩展。

examples.en: The school tried to civilize the children of the frontier.
examples.cn: 这所学校试图教化边疆地区的孩子。

examples.en: He was civilized by years of travel and good company.
examples.cn: 多年的旅行与良好的交往让他变得文雅。

examples.en: Missionaries came to civilize the islanders and stayed to learn from them.
examples.cn: 传教士来教化岛民，后来却留下来向他们学习。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 civil 想成「市民的」，ize 想成「使」：使人都像市民那样守规矩，就是教化。

root: 源自拉丁语 civilis（公民的），经法语 civiliser 进入英语，字面意思是使某人变得像公民一样守秩序。

sensesIntro.en: The verb first improves a whole society, then a single person's manners.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词先指改善整个社会，再指改善个人的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road, a school and a court rising on open land.
core.cn: 核心意象：开阔土地上同时立起道路、学校与法庭。

branches.en: The verb pushes a whole society towards cities and law.
branches.cn: 这个动词把整个社会推向城市与法律。

branches.en: The same verb polishes the manners of one person.
branches.cn: 同一个动词也打磨个人的举止。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of making someone fit for society.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享让某人适合社会的意思。

branches.en: Trade and schools do the work that the verb describes.
branches.cn: 贸易与学校承担了这个动词所描述的工作。

branches.en: Manners are the small private form of the public process.
branches.cn: 举止是这一公共过程在私人层面的小形态。

intro.en: The verb base takes the -ize ending and grows a noun and two adjectives.
intro.cn: 这个动词词基接 -ize 后缀，并长出名词与两个形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin civilis, so the verb belongs to the same citizen family as civil and civilian.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 civilis，因此这个动词与 civil、civilian 同属公民家族。

items.meaning: to bring a society to a developed stage
items.example: Steam ships helped civilize the coast.
items.exampleCN: 汽船帮助沿海走向文明。

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject
items.exampleCN: 贸易很快使港口文明起来。

items.example: The railway civilized the valley in ten years.
items.exampleCN: 铁路在十年间使山谷文明起来。

items.meaning: used for perfect tenses and the passive
items.meaningCN: 用于完成时与被动语态
items.example: The region was civilized by settlers.
items.exampleCN: 这一地区被移民开化了。

items.example: They were civilizing the frontier slowly.
The verb gave birth to civilization.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词孕育出文明一词。
礼貌的回答不花什么成本。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示使之怎样的动词

latinEntries.example: Civilis is the base of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: civilis 是整个家族的词基。

definition_zh: 小屋；棚屋
definition_en: a small simple building, often made of wood
core_image: 田边一间木屋，屋顶压着石块
scene: 农夫在田边搭了一间小屋。 The farmer built a hut at the edge of the field.

senses.title: A small simple house

definition_zh: 手写；亲笔书写
definition_en: to write something by hand rather than by typing or printing
core_image: 笔尖在纸上一笔一画地移动
scene: 请手写这封信。 Please handwrite this letter.
sceneCN: 这里 handwrite 是「手写」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请手写这封信。

senses.title: Write by hand
senses.definition: to write with a pen or pencil rather than a machine
senses.definitionCN: 用笔而不是机器书写
senses.example: Please handwrite this letter.
senses.exampleCN: 请手写这封信。
senses.why: Writing by hand is the plain sense.

senses.title: Write yourself

senses.example: The author handwrote every draft.

senses.why: The sense stresses the writer's own hand.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项强调书写者本人的手。

intro.en: Handwrite joins hand with write, both Old English words.
intro.cn: handwrite 由 hand 与 write 两个古英语词组合而成。

items.en: Hand meant the hand.

sensesIntro.en: Handwrite means to write by hand, or to write something personally.

definition_zh: 词汇；词汇量；词语表；术语
definition_en: all the words that a person knows or that a language uses
core_image: 一叠被翻得卷角的单词卡片，从薄薄几张变成厚厚一捆
scene: 老师让学生每天在卡片上写几个新词，期末数一数，那厚厚一叠就是这一学期的收获。 Reading widely is the surest way to build a larger vocabulary.
sceneCN: 这里 vocabulary 是「词汇量」（第 1 个义项：一个人掌握或一种语言使用的全部词）；句意为广泛阅读是扩大词汇量最可靠的办法。卷角卡片叠成一捆的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: All the words a person knows
senses.definition: the stock of words that one person can understand and use
senses.definitionCN: 一个人能理解与使用的全部词
senses.example: Reading widely is the surest way to build a larger vocabulary.
senses.exampleCN: 广泛阅读是扩大词汇量最可靠的办法。
senses.why: The Latin seed meant a naming or a calling, and a set of names one owns is exactly a personal word stock.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「命名」或「称呼」，一个人所拥有的名字集合正是他的词库。

senses.title: The words of a language or field
senses.titleCN: （某一语言或领域的）词汇；术语
senses.definition: the whole set of words used by a language, a subject or a group
senses.definitionCN: 一种语言、一个学科或一个群体所使用的全部词
senses.example: The vocabulary of chemistry is full of Greek compounds.
senses.exampleCN: 化学的词汇里满是希腊语的合成词。
senses.why: A trade names its own objects, so the collection of names grows into a field’s word stock.
senses.whyCN: 一个行业要为自家的事物命名，于是「名字的集合」长成了某一领域的词库。

senses.title: A list of words to be learned
senses.definition: a list of words with meanings, often arranged for study
senses.definitionCN: 带释义、常按学习次序编排的词表
senses.example: Each unit opens with a short vocabulary at the back of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 每个单元都在页后附一小段词汇表。
senses.why: Books printed such a list under the same name, and so the collection became the page you study from.
senses.whyCN: 书本也把这样的清单一并叫作这个名字，于是「汇集」变成了你研读的那一页。

senses.title: The range of expressive signs
senses.definition: the set of forms or gestures used by an art, a style or a machine, in extended use
senses.definitionCN: 在引申用法中指某种艺术、风格或机器使用的形式与语汇
senses.example: The painter kept a limited vocabulary of shapes and colours.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家只用有限的一套形状与色彩语汇。
senses.why: Once a stock of words is a set of available signs, any art with recurring forms can be said to have one.
senses.whyCN: 一旦词库被看作可用的符号集合，任何有反复形式的艺术都可以说拥有它。

intro.en: Vocabulary goes back to Latin vocare, to call, through the noun vocabulum, a name.
intro.cn: vocabulary 上溯到拉丁语 vocare（呼叫），经由名词 vocabulum（名称）。

items.en: Vocare meant to call or to name, and a vocabulum was a name, one called thing.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼叫或称呼，vocabulum 就是一个名称、一个被叫到的东西。

items.en: Medieval Latin used vocabularium for a collection of names or words, a word list.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 vocabularium 指名称或词语的汇集，即词表。

items.en: The plural vocabula covered the stock of names someone or something had.
items.cn: 复数 vocabula 指某人或某物所拥有的「名字」总和。

items.en: French vocabulary passed into English in the sixteenth century, at first as a list of hard words.
items.cn: 法语的词汇一语在十六世纪进入英语，起初指难词的清单。

items.en: The sense then grew from the list to the whole stock of words, personal or shared.
items.cn: 此后词义从「清单」扩大到全部词的总和，可属个人，也可共享。

note.en: The first group gathers the calling root, the second the words that overlap with vocabulary in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收「呼叫」词根，第二组收与 vocabulary 意义重叠的词。
