definition_zh: 湿气；水分；潮气；含水量
definition_en: small amounts of water held on a surface, in the air, in soil or inside a material
core_image: 清晨的岩壁上凝着一层看不见的水汽，手指摸上去凉而微湿
scene: 清晨的岩壁上蒙着一层细水汽，摸上去凉凉的。 Dew had left a thin film of moisture on the rock face.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「物体表面少量附着的水分」（第 1 个义项：表面的一层薄水）；句意为露水在岩壁上留下了一层薄薄的水汽；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A thin film of water on a surface
senses.titleCN: 物体表面附着的一层薄水
senses.definition: a small amount of water lying on the surface of an object
senses.definitionCN: 附着在物体表面的一层少量水
senses.example: Dew had left a thin film of moisture on the rock face.
senses.exampleCN: 露水在岩壁上留下了一层薄薄的水汽。
senses.why: Moisture never names a body of water; it names water only as something small, held by a surface and waiting to evaporate.
senses.whyCN: moisture 从不指一片水域，只指被表面挽留、随时会蒸发掉的一点点水。

senses.title: Water vapour held in the air
senses.definition: water in the form of vapour that is present in the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 以水汽形式存在大气中的水分
senses.example: The air in the greenhouse keeps enough moisture for the seedlings.
senses.exampleCN: 温室里的空气保持了足够幼苗生长的水汽。
senses.why: Air can hold water invisibly; when people speak of moisture in the air they mean this invisible load, not rain.
senses.whyCN: 空气能看不见地含水；说空气中的 moisture，指的是这份看不见的含水，而不是下雨。

senses.title: Water stored in soil
senses.definition: water held between soil particles and available to plant roots
senses.definitionCN: 保存在土壤颗粒之间、可供根系利用的水
senses.example: Mulch holds moisture in the soil through the dry months.
senses.exampleCN: 覆盖物在干旱的月份里把水分留在土壤中。
senses.why: Soil is another surface that can hold small amounts of water, so the same word extends from rock to earth.
senses.whyCN: 土壤也是能挽留少量水的表面，于是同一个词从岩石延伸到土地。

senses.title: Water content of food or material
senses.titleCN: 食物或材料内部的含水量
senses.definition: the water contained inside a substance such as grain, wood or plaster
senses.definitionCN: 谷物、木材、灰泥等物质内部所含的水
senses.example: The mill checks the moisture of every sack of grain before milling.
senses.exampleCN: 磨坊在研磨前检查每一袋谷物的含水量。
senses.why: Here the water is inside, not on the surface, but it is still a measured quantity that the material holds.
senses.whyCN: 这里的水在内部而不在表面，但仍然是材料所持有、可被计量的一份水。

senses.title: Water kept in living skin
senses.definition: the water naturally held in skin or hair, often spoken of in cosmetics
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤或头发中天然保持的水，常见于护肤语境
senses.example: This cream seals moisture into dry skin.
senses.exampleCN: 这款乳霜把水分锁在干燥的皮肤里。
senses.why: Living tissue is a moist surface, so its water became the standard subject of the word in skin-care writing.
senses.whyCN: 活体组织本身就是湿润的表面，因此护肤写作把皮肤里的水当成了这个词的固定对象。

senses.title: Condensation on a cold surface
senses.titleCN: 遇冷凝结在表面上的水
senses.definition: droplets that form when warm damp air meets a cold surface
senses.definitionCN: 暖湿空气遇到冷表面时凝结成的小水珠
senses.example: Moisture ran down the window in the warm kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 温暖的厨房里，水汽顺着窗玻璃往下流。
senses.why: This is the surface film again, but now produced by a temperature difference rather than by dew.
senses.whyCN: 这仍是表面那层水膜，只是成因从露水变成了温差。

senses.title: A measured water ratio
senses.titleCN: 作为仪器读数的含水率
senses.definition: the percentage of water in a material, measured for engineering or trade
senses.definitionCN: 为工程或交易测定出的材料含水百分比
senses.example: Engineers record the moisture content of the concrete before pouring.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在浇筑前记录混凝土的含水率。
senses.why: Once a value can be weighed and printed, the word turns into a number on a gauge.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这份水能被称量、打印出来，这个词就变成了仪表上的一个数字。

senses.title: Dampness as a building problem
senses.titleCN: 建筑中造成损坏的潮气
senses.definition: unwanted water inside walls or floors that damages a building
senses.definitionCN: 侵入墙体或地板、造成损坏的多余水分
senses.example: Moisture in the walls had softened the old plaster.
senses.exampleCN: 墙里的潮气早把旧灰泥泡软了。
senses.why: The same water that keeps a plant alive ruins plaster; when the holder is a building, the word turns into a fault.
senses.whyCN: 同一份水能养活植物，也能毁掉灰泥；当持有者是房屋时，这个词就变成了一个毛病。

intro.en: The word reached English through Old French, and its deeper Latin source is disputed. Dates are approximate and the contested step is marked.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语进入英语，更早的拉丁来源存在争议。年代为大致估计，存疑的一环已明确标注。

items.en: Old French moistour 'moisture, dampness' was formed from moiste 'moist, wet' plus the noun suffix -our, from Latin -ura.
items.cn: 古法语 moistour「湿气、潮湿」由 moiste「湿的」加名词后缀 -our（出自拉丁 -ura）构成。

items.en: English borrowed the noun as moisture and used it first for dampness in air, soil and stored goods.
items.cn: 英语借入为 moisture，最早用于空气、土壤和储存货物中的潮气。

items.en: The adjective behind moist is usually reconstructed as Vulgar Latin *muscidus 'mouldy', an altered form of Latin mucidus. This reconstruction is a hypothesis, not a recorded form.
items.cn: moist 背后的形容词通常被重构为俗拉丁语 *muscidus「发霉的」，是拉丁语 mucidus 的变形。这一重构只是假说，并非有记录的形式。

items.en: Some scholars instead connect the Romance words to Latin madere 'to be wet' and madidus 'wet'. The two explanations are usually listed side by side; the source of moist is marked as source uncertain.
items.cn: 也有学者把这一组罗曼语词联系到拉丁语 madere「潮湿」和 madidus「湿的」。两种解释通常并列，moist 的来源不确定。

items.en: With the growth of agriculture, food processing and engineering, moisture came to mean a measurable water content rather than only a feeling of dampness.
items.cn: 随着农业、食品加工和工程的发展，moisture 逐渐指可测量的含水量，而不只是潮湿的感觉。

note.en: Group one holds forms that look or sound close to moisture; group two holds words that also name water held somewhere.
note.cn: 第一组是与 moisture 字形或读音接近的词；第二组是也指「某处所含的水」的词。

entries.definition: The comparative of the adjective moist, meaning more damp. It belongs to the same family and adds -er, not -ure.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词 moist 的比较级，表示更湿润。它属同一词族，词尾是 -er 而不是 -ure。

entries.definition: A combination of two or more substances. The middle consonant is -xt-, and the word comes from Latin miscere 'to mix', not from moist.
entries.definitionCN: 两种或多种物质的混合物。中间是 -xt-，源自拉丁语 miscere「混合」，与 moist 无关。

entries.definition: A cream that adds water to the skin; it is moisture plus -ize plus -er, so the ending is long and the meaning is a product.
entries.definitionCN: 给皮肤补水的乳霜；由 moisture 加 -ize 再加 -er 构成，词尾更长，指的是产品。

entries.definition: A mildly unpleasant wetness in air or in a material; it often carries a hint of discomfort that moisture does not.
entries.definitionCN: 空气或材料中令人略感不适的微湿；常带 moisture 所没有的不适意味。

entries.definition: The amount of water vapour in the air, usually reported as a percentage; it is the technical measure of atmospheric moisture.
entries.definitionCN: 空气中的水汽量，通常以百分比报告，是大气水分的技术指标。

entries.definition: The process by which vapour turns into liquid, or the drops produced; moisture on a window is its visible result.
entries.definitionCN: 水汽变成液体的过程，或由此产生的水珠；窗上的水汽就是它的可见结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes and real compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：使用真实的后缀与真实的复合词，不编造顺口溜。

normal.en: moist + -ure: -ure is a noun suffix seen in pressure and departure, so the adjective 'wet' becomes the noun 'wetness'.
normal.cn: moist + -ure：-ure 是名词后缀（如 pressure、departure），于是形容词「湿的」变成名词「湿气」。

normal.en: moisten = moist + -en, the suffix that turns adjectives into verbs of making, as in widen and deepen.
normal.cn: moisten = moist + -en，这个后缀把形容词变成「使……」的动词，如 widen、deepen。

normal.en: moisturize = moisture + -ize, 'to put moisture into', and a moisturizer is the thing that does it.
normal.cn: moisturize = moisture + -ize，意为「把水分放进去」；moisturizer 就是做这件事的东西。

normal.en: moisture-proof = moisture + -proof 'resistant to', the same pattern as waterproof and fireproof.
normal.cn: moisture-proof = moisture + -proof「防……的」，与 waterproof、fireproof 同构。

normal.en: The fixed phrases soil moisture and moisture content turn invisible water into something a farmer or engineer can measure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配 soil moisture 与 moisture content 把看不见的水变成农民或工程师可以测量的东西。

abstract.en: Abstractly, moisture is water that has stopped moving: no river, no wave, only a film clinging to a surface. Symbol: a grey stone with one shining skin.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，moisture 是停止流动的水：不是河，不是浪，只是贴在表面上的一层膜。符号：一块灰石头上裹着一层发亮的薄皮。

abstract.en: The same film can live in air, in earth, in wood or in skin; the holder changes, the amount stays small.
abstract.cn: 同一层膜可以住在空气、泥土、木头或皮肤里；容器在变，量始终很小。

abstract.en: So moisture is not 'water' but 'water held'; the word always asks where it is kept and how much remains.
abstract.cn: 所以 moisture 不是「水」，而是「被留住的水」；这个词总在追问：它被存在哪里，还剩多少。

examples.en: A sealed jar keeps the moisture in the tobacco from escaping.
examples.cn: 密封的罐子能防止烟草里的水分跑掉。

examples.en: Farmers dig shallow pits to trap moisture during the dry season.
examples.cn: 农民在旱季挖浅坑来留住水分。

examples.en: The forecast warns that moisture from the gulf will bring heavy rain.
examples.cn: 预报提醒来自墨西哥湾的水汽将带来大雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「抹湿的」：抹一下，表面就湿了 → moisture 湿气、水分

root: 古法语 moistour「湿气」← moiste「湿的」；再往前通常重构为俗拉丁语 *muscidus「发霉的」，也有人联系拉丁语 madere「潮湿」，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: a small amount of water held by something. It starts on a surface, moves into air and soil, enters materials and skin, appears as condensation, becomes a measured ratio, and finally counts as damage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个意思展开：被某物留住的一点点水。它从表面开始，进入空气与土壤，进入材料与皮肤，又以凝结水的形态出现，随后变成可测的比值，最后被视为一种损坏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a little water that cannot flow away because a surface or a body holds it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一点无法流走的水，因为某个表面或物体把它留住了。

branches.en: VISIBLE FILM: dew on rock and condensation on glass are the same skin of water, produced by two different causes.
branches.cn: 可见水膜：岩石上的露与玻璃上的凝结水是同一层水皮，只是成因不同。

branches.en: HIDDEN HOLDERS: air and soil carry water without showing it, one as vapour and one between particles.
branches.cn: 隐形容器：空气与土壤都不显形地带着水，一个以水汽，一个在颗粒之间。

branches.en: INSIDE A SUBSTANCE: grain and concrete hold water that trade and engineering want as a number.
branches.cn: 物质内部：谷物与混凝土所含的水，是交易与工程想要的一个数字。

branches.en: LIVING TISSUE: skin and hair hold water that cosmetics try to keep in place.
branches.cn: 活体组织：皮肤与头发所含的水，是护肤品想留住的东西。

branches.en: FAULT: the same water becomes a defect when the holder is a wall or a floor.
branches.cn: 毛病：当容器是墙或地板时，同一份水就成了缺陷。

intro.en: Moisture sits at the centre of a small family of suffixes: -ure makes the noun, -en and -ize make verbs, -ness makes a quality, and -proof makes a defence.
intro.cn: moisture 处在一个小词族的中心：-ure 造名词，-en 与 -ize 造动词，-ness 造性质名词，-proof 造防护形容词。

latinIntro.en: Moist and moisture came through Old French, and the Latin step behind them is disputed. Because no Latin source can be stated safely, the Latin entry list is left empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: moist 与 moisture 经古法语而来，其背后的拉丁环节存在争议。由于无法稳妥地给出拉丁来源，拉丁词条列表按设计留空。

items.meaning: made so that damp cannot get in or out
items.example: The seeds are packed in moisture-proof foil.
items.exampleCN: 种子被装在防潮的铝箔袋里。

items.meaning: able to pull sweat or water away from a surface
items.meaningCN: 吸湿排汗的（wick 指把液体吸走）
items.exampleCN: 跑者更爱穿吸湿排汗的袜子。

items.meaning: to add water to the skin or hair
items.meaningCN: 给皮肤或头发补水（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: She moisturizes her hands after every wash.
items.exampleCN: 她每次洗手后都会给手补水。

items.meaning: a product that adds water to the skin
items.meaningCN: 保湿霜；润肤品（-er 表示做该动作的东西）
items.example: Use a light moisturizer under sunscreen.
items.exampleCN: 防晒霜下面先涂一层清爽的保湿霜。

items.meaningCN: 使微湿；沾湿（-en 表示「使……」）
items.example: Moisten the clay before you shape it.
items.exampleCN: 塑形之前先把黏土弄湿。

items.meaning: the quality of being slightly wet
items.meaningCN: 湿润；潮湿（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The moistness of the cake depends on the flour.
items.exampleCN: 蛋糕的湿润程度取决于面粉。

items.meaning: slightly wet, often in a pleasant way
items.meaningCN: 微湿的（常带宜人的意味），是本词族的基础形容词
items.example: The cake stays moist for three days.
items.exampleCN: 这块蛋糕能保持湿润三天。

items.meaning: water held in the ground, studied in farming and hydrology
items.meaningCN: 土壤水分（soil 与 moisture 构成的复合术语）
items.example: Sensors log soil moisture every hour.
items.exampleCN: 传感器每小时记录一次土壤水分。

definition_zh: 相互的；彼此的；共同的（后一义常被批评为宽松用法）
definition_en: given, felt, or done by each side toward the other in exchange; also shared in common by two or more parties
core_image: 两只手同时递出同一把钥匙：你给我，我也给你
scene: 两位邻居隔着栅栏交换对方大门的钥匙，各替对方保管一把备用钥匙。 Two neighbours stand at the fence and hand each other a key to the other's gate; their help is mutual, since each one keeps a spare key for the other.
sceneCN: 这里 mutual 是「互相给予、彼此交换」（第 1 个义项：两方对等地给出并接受）；句意：两位邻居站在篱笆边，各自把对方院门的钥匙递给对方，他们的帮助是相互的，因为各自都为对方留了一把备用钥匙。图中可辨识物件：木篱笆、两把钥匙、两只同时伸出的手、两扇院门；对应第 1 个义项。

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 互助主义者；互利共生的
使共有；把（企业）转为互助制

senses.title: Reciprocally given: both sides exchange
senses.titleCN: 互相给予：两边都在交换
senses.definition: given by each side to the other, so that what one gives is returned in kind
senses.definitionCN: 一方给出的，另一方也以同类回报；给予与接受同时发生在两边
senses.example: Their help was mutual: each repaired what the other had broken.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的帮助是相互的：各自修好了对方弄坏的东西。
senses.why: Late 15c. mutual was first used of feelings and meant 'reciprocally given and received'. The core picture is an exchange: I give, you give back.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪晚期 mutual 最先用于感情，义为“相互给予并接受”。核心画面是一次交换：我给，你也给回来。

senses.title: Mutual affection: a feeling each holds for the other
senses.titleCN: 相互的情感：各自对对方怀有同样的心
senses.definition: of a feeling, held by two people each toward the other, so that the regard is returned
senses.definitionCN: 指一种情感，两人各自对对方怀有，因而这份心意是被回应的
senses.example: The mutual affection between the two sisters lasted all their lives.
senses.exampleCN: 两姐妹之间的相互关爱持续了一生。
senses.why: A feeling can itself be the thing exchanged. Each heart holds the same regard, so the emotion is returned rather than held on one side only.
senses.whyCN: 情感本身就可以是被交换的东西。两颗心怀着同样的心意，因此这份情感是被回应的，而不是只停留在一边。

senses.title: The disputed mutual friend: a person known to both
senses.titleCN: 备受争议的 mutual friend：两人都认识的人
senses.definition: a person whom two other people both know, whether or not those two know each other through that person
senses.definitionCN: 两个人都认识的人，不论这两人是否正因此人而相识
senses.example: We met through a mutual friend at the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 我们经一位共同的朋友在博物馆相识。
senses.why: The 1630s 'common' sense let mutual describe what two parties share. Victorian critics attacked a mutual friend because a friend is not exchanged, yet the phrase is now standard.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 30 年代出现的“共同”义，让 mutual 可以形容两方共享之物。维多利亚时代的批评者攻击 a mutual friend，因为朋友并不是被“交换”的；但这一说法如今已属标准。

senses.title: Shared in common: a quality both possess
senses.titleCN: 共同拥有：两方都具有的性质
senses.definition: held or possessed in common by two or more parties, with no idea of exchange
senses.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同持有或拥有，不含交换之意
senses.example: Their mutual interest in birds began at the same observatory.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对鸟类的共同兴趣始于同一座观测站。
senses.why: From the 1630s mutual widened from exchange to possession: two parties hold the same thing. This branch is the loose 'common' use that style guides still argue about.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪 30 年代起，mutual 从“交换”扩展到“持有”：两方握着同一样东西。这条分支就是用法指南至今仍在争论的宽松“共同”义。

senses.title: Mutual benefit: advantage that runs both ways
senses.definition: producing advantage for each of the parties involved, so that neither gains at the other's expense
senses.definitionCN: 为涉及的每一方都带来好处，没有一方以另一方受损为代价获利
senses.example: The trade deal was based on mutual benefit rather than charity.
senses.exampleCN: 这项贸易协定建立在互利而非施舍之上。
senses.why: Benefit follows the exchange image: each side hands over something and receives something in return, so the gain travels in both directions.
senses.whyCN: benefit 延续了交换意象：每一方交出一些东西，又得到一些回报，因此好处是双向流动的。

senses.title: Mutual agreement: a promise binding both sides
senses.titleCN: 双方协议：约束两边的承诺
senses.definition: an arrangement accepted by both parties and binding each of them equally
senses.definitionCN: 两方都接受、并同等约束双方的安排
senses.example: They ended the lease by mutual agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 他们经双方同意终止了租约。
senses.why: An agreement is exchanged as promises: each gives a pledge and receives one. Because both are bound, the obligation is mutual in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: 协议是以承诺作交换：各方给出一份保证，也收到一份保证。由于双方都受约束，这种义务是严格意义上的“相互的”。

senses.title: Mutual insurance: a company owned by its members
senses.titleCN: 互助保险：由会员共同拥有的公司
senses.definition: of an insurer or society owned by its policyholders, who share the risks and the profits
senses.definitionCN: 指由保单持有人共同拥有的保险机构，成员分担风险、共享收益
senses.example: The mutual insurance society returned part of the premium to every member.
senses.exampleCN: 这家互助保险社把部分保费返还给每位成员。
senses.why: Members pay in and cover one another, so the exchange is pooled rather than one-to-one. Mutual names the arrangement in which each member is both payer and owner.
senses.whyCN: 成员缴钱并相互保障，交换因此被汇聚起来，而不是一对一进行。mutual 命名的是这样一种安排：每个成员既是付款人又是所有者。

senses.title: Mutual fund: money pooled and shared
senses.titleCN: 共同基金：汇集并共享的资金
senses.definition: a fund in which many investors pool money and share the returns, recorded from 1950
senses.definitionCN: 众多投资者汇集资金并共享收益的基金，该说法记录于 1950 年
senses.example: She put her savings into a mutual fund rather than a single stock.
senses.exampleCN: 她把积蓄投入共同基金，而不是单只股票。
senses.why: Here mutual marks a pool: every investor holds a share of the same whole. The exchange is between members and the fund, and the ownership is shared.
senses.whyCN: 这里 mutual 标记的是一口“资金池”：每位投资者都持有同一整体的份额。交换发生在成员与基金之间，所有权则是共享的。

senses.title: Mutual relation: each term implies the other
senses.titleCN: 相互关系：每一项都蕴含另一项
senses.definition: in logic and mathematics, of a relation in which each of two terms entails or points to the other
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑与数学中，指两项之间每一项都蕴含或指向另一项的关系
senses.example: In logic, entailment is mutual when each of two propositions follows from the other.
senses.exampleCN: 在逻辑中，当两个命题各自都能推出对方时，蕴含关系就是相互的。
senses.why: The exchange becomes formal: A gives support to B and B gives support back to A. Mutual relation names this perfect two-way dependency.
senses.whyCN: 交换在这里变得形式化：A 给 B 支撑，B 也给 A 支撑。mutual relation 命名的是这种完美的双向依赖。

senses.title: Mutual assured destruction: a guarantee aimed both ways
senses.titleCN: 相互确保摧毁：对准两边的保证
senses.definition: the Cold War doctrine that a full nuclear exchange would destroy both sides, so neither would strike first; abbreviated MAD in 1966
senses.definitionCN: 冷战理论：全面核交换将摧毁双方，因此谁都不敢先动手；1966 年缩写为 MAD
senses.example: Mutual assured destruction gave the Cold War its strangest acronym, MAD.
senses.exampleCN: 相互确保摧毁给冷战留下了最古怪的缩写 MAD。
senses.why: Each side guarantees the other's destruction, so the threat is returned in full. The word's exchange core hardens into a deadly symmetry.
senses.whyCN: 每一方都保证对方的毁灭，威胁被完整地回敬过去。这个词的“交换”核心在这里硬化成一种致命的对称。

intro.en: Mutual entered English in the late 15c. from Old French mutuel, and its first sense was an exchange of feeling, not joint ownership. The 'common' sense is a later and often criticised extension.
intro.cn: mutual 于 15 世纪晚期从古法语 mutuel 进入英语，最初的义项是情感的交换，而不是共同拥有。“共同”义是后来出现、且常受批评的扩展。

items.en: First recorded in the late 15c., used of feelings in the sense 'reciprocally given and received'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 15 世纪晚期，用于感情，义为“相互给予并接受”。

items.en: From Old French mutuel (14c.), which passed the Latin adjective into French.
items.cn: 来自古法语 mutuel（14 世纪），该词把拉丁语形容词带入了法语。

items.en: Latin mutuus meant 'reciprocal, done in exchange'; the stem mut- carries the idea of change and exchange.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mutuus 意为“相互的、交换而成的”；词干 mut- 带有“改变、交换”的意思。

items.en: Traced to PIE *mei-(1) 'to change, go, move'. Watkins adds that its derivatives concern goods and services exchanged by custom or law.
items.cn: 可追溯至原始印欧语 *mei-(1)“改变、去、移动”。Watkins 补充说，该词根的衍生词与社会中按习俗或法律进行的货物与服务交换有关。

items.en: The sense 'common, shared' appears in the 1630s and was already noted as loosely misused, especially in a mutual friend.
items.cn: “共同的、共享的”义在 17 世纪 30 年代出现，当时就已被指出常被宽松误用，尤其见于 a mutual friend。

items.en: Mutual fund is recorded from 1950 and mutual assured destruction, or MAD, from 1966; both keep the two-way picture.
items.cn: mutual fund 记录于 1950 年，mutual assured destruction（缩写 MAD）记录于 1966 年；两者都保留了双向的画面。

note.en: The first group shares the mut- stem or sound, the second shares the meaning of two-way or shared, so form and sense stay apart.
note.cn: 第一组共享 mut- 词干或读音，第二组共享“双向／共享”的词义，这样词形与词义不会被混为一谈。

entries.definition: liable to change. It comes from Latin mutare 'to change', the same PIE family as mutuus, but means changeable rather than exchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 易变的。它来自拉丁语 mutare“改变”，与 mutuus 同属一个原始印欧语词族，但意思是“可变的”，不是“被交换的”。

entries.definition: a change of form or genetic material. It is built on mutare 'to change', not on mutuus 'reciprocal'.
entries.definitionCN: 形态改变；基因突变。它建立在 mutare“改变”上，而不是 mutuus“相互的”上。

entries.definition: to travel regularly to work, or to reduce a punishment. It comes from Latin commutare 'to exchange, change', com- plus mutare.
entries.definitionCN: 通勤；减刑。它来自拉丁语 commutare“交换、改变”，由 com- 加 mutare 构成。

entries.definition: given or done by each side to the other. It is the strict term for the exchange sense, while mutual also covers shared possession.
entries.definitionCN: 相互给予或做出的。它是“交换”义的严格说法，而 mutual 还覆盖“共同拥有”。

entries.definition: belonging to or shared by several. It states joint possession without any idea of giving and receiving.
entries.definitionCN: 共有的；共同使用的。它只说明共同拥有，不含给予与接受的意思。

entries.definition: done or shared by two or more parties acting together, as in a joint statement.
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同做出或共享的，如 joint statement（联合声明）。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin stem mut-, the mutare family of mutable and mutation, and the documented history of mutual friend, mutual fund and MAD.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁词干 mut-、mutable 与 mutation 所属的 mutare 词族，以及 mutual friend、mutual fund、MAD 有据可查的历史。

normal.en: Picture an exchange: one hand gives a key, the other hand gives a key back. That is the original sense, 'reciprocally given and received'.
normal.cn: 想象一次交换：一只手递出钥匙，另一只手也递回钥匙。这就是本义“相互给予并接受”。

normal.en: Mutable, mutation and commute all carry Latin mutare 'to change'; mutual carries the same stem for an exchange of things or feelings.
normal.cn: mutable、mutation、commute 都带拉丁语 mutare“改变”；mutual 用同一词干表示物品或情感的交换。

normal.en: A mutual friend is a person both parties know, which is why critics call the phrase a loose use of 'common'.
normal.cn: a mutual friend 是两方都认识的人，正因如此，批评者说这个短语是对 common 的宽松误用。

normal.en: A mutual fund pools money, and mutual insurance pools risk: both are modern institutions built on shared ownership.
normal.cn: mutual fund 汇集资金，mutual insurance 汇集风险：两者都是建立在共同所有权上的现代制度。

normal.en: The standard frames are mutual respect, mutual understanding, mutual benefit and mutual agreement.
normal.cn: 标准搭配是 mutual respect、mutual understanding、mutual benefit 与 mutual agreement。

abstract.en: Two arrows drawn head to head: each direction needs the other, and a single arrow would not be mutual.
abstract.cn: 画两支箭头对着彼此：每个方向都需要另一边，只画一支就不叫 mutual。

abstract.en: A two-pan balance with equal weights: nothing tips, because what is given on one side is returned on the other.
abstract.cn: 一架两盘天平，两边砝码相等：哪边都不下沉，因为一边给出的在另一边被回敬。

abstract.en: Take one partner away and the word loses its point: mutual always needs a second party in the picture.
abstract.cn: 拿走一方，这个词就失去意义：mutual 的画面里永远需要一个“另一方”。

examples.en: The two countries signed the treaty out of mutual interest, not friendship.
examples.cn: 两国签署这项条约是出于共同利益，而非友谊。

examples.en: Mutual respect kept the debate civil even when the disagreement was sharp.
examples.cn: 相互尊重让这场辩论即使分歧尖锐也保持文明。

examples.en: They were introduced by a mutual friend who knew both families.
examples.cn: 他们是由一位认识两家人的共同朋友引见的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谬球」——两人把同一个球互相抛来抛去，你抛给我、我抛给你 → mutual 相互的、彼此的

root: 源自拉丁语 mutuus“相互的、交换而成的”，可追溯至原始印欧语 *mei-(1)“改变、移动”，核心是双方交换，而非共同拥有。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of mutual all grow from one picture: two parties handing something to each other. From exchanged feeling it extends to shared possession, then to contracts, member-owned institutions, formal relations and finally to the deadly symmetry of MAD.
sensesIntro.cn: mutual 的十个义项都从同一幅画生长出来：两方把东西递给对方。从被交换的情感，它扩展到共同拥有，再扩展到契约、会员共有的机构、形式关系，最后到 MAD 那种致命的对称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands passing the same key to each other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手把同一把钥匙互相递过去。

branches.en: THE EXCHANGE CORE: reciprocal action and reciprocal feeling, the oldest and strictest sense.
branches.cn: 交换核心：相互的行为与相互的情感，最古老也最严格的义项。

branches.en: SHARED, NOT EXCHANGED: the disputed mutual friend and the wider 'common' sense.
branches.cn: 共享而非交换：备受争议的 mutual friend，以及更宽的“共同”义。

branches.en: BENEFIT AND CONTRACT: advantage that runs both ways, and promises that bind both sides.
branches.cn: 利益与契约：双向流动的好处，以及约束双方的承诺。

branches.en: POOLED OWNERSHIP: member-owned insurance and the mutual fund, where sharing becomes an institution.
branches.cn: 汇聚式所有权：会员共有的保险与共同基金，共享在此变成制度。

branches.en: FORMAL SYMMETRY: mutual entailment in logic and the mutual destruction of the nuclear standoff.
branches.cn: 形式对称：逻辑中的相互蕴含，以及核对峙中的相互摧毁。

intro.en: Mutual is Latin mutuus plus the adjective suffix -al. English then builds mutually, mutuality, mutualism, mutualist, mutualize and mutualization, while the bare stem mut- lives on in mutation, mutable and commute.
intro.cn: mutual 是拉丁语 mutuus 加形容词后缀 -al。英语随后构造出 mutually、mutuality、mutualism、mutualist、mutualize 与 mutualization，而光秃的词干 mut- 仍活在 mutation、mutable、commute 中。

latinIntro.en: Latin mutuus 'reciprocal, done in exchange' is the direct source; the same stem gives mutare 'to change' and commutare 'to exchange'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mutuus“相互的、交换而成的”是直接来源；同一词干还给出 mutare“改变”与 commutare“交换”。

items.meaningCN: 相互的；双方共享的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The agreement rests on mutual trust.
items.exampleCN: 这项协议建立在相互信任之上。

items.meaning: in a reciprocal way, each toward the other
items.meaningCN: 相互地；彼此地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two plans are mutually exclusive.

items.meaningCN: 相互性；共同性（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The contract depends on the mutuality of the promises.
items.exampleCN: 这份合同依赖于承诺的相互性。

items.meaning: a system of mutual dependence, or a symbiotic partnership
items.meaningCN: 互助主义；互利共生（-ism 构成体系名词）
items.example: Certain ants and plants live in mutualism.
items.exampleCN: 某些蚂蚁与植物处于互利共生关系。

items.meaning: a supporter of mutualism, or an organism in a mutual partnership
items.meaningCN: 互助主义者；互利共生的一方（-ist 构成人或形容词）
items.example: The coral and its algae are mutualists.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚与它的藻类是互利共生的一方。

items.meaning: to convert an enterprise into member ownership
items.meaningCN: 使共有；转为互助制（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The society voted to mutualize the savings bank.
items.exampleCN: 该协会投票决定把储蓄银行转为互助制。

items.meaningCN: 共有化；互助化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Mutualization changed how the insurer was governed.
items.exampleCN: 互助化改变了这家保险公司的治理方式。

items.meaning: a change of form or genetic material
items.example: The mutation gave the moths a darker wing.
items.exampleCN: 这次突变让蛾子的翅膀变深了。

items.meaningCN: 易变的；可改变的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: Language is mutable, and slang changes fastest.
items.exampleCN: 语言是可变的，而俚语变化最快。

items.meaning: to travel regularly, or to exchange one penalty for another
items.meaningCN: 通勤；减刑（com-“共同、交换”+ mut-“改变”）
items.example: She commutes by train every morning.
items.exampleCN: 她每天早上乘火车通勤。

definition_zh: 受欢迎；人气；普及程度；声望
definition_en: the state of being liked or supported by many people, and the degree to which something is widely accepted
core_image: 一块电子屏上的数字不断往上跳，屏幕前的店主抬头看了三次
scene: 新开的面包店在社交平台上被反复转发，门口的队伍从早到晚没有断过。 The popularity of the little bakery surprised even its owner.
sceneCN: 这里 popularity 指「受欢迎的程度」（第 1 个义项：被很多人喜欢的状况）；句意为这家小面包店的火爆连店主自己都感到意外。图中可辨识场景：不断上涨的数字、从早排到晚的队伍、反复转发的手机屏幕。

pos.zh: 受欢迎；人气；普及程度；声望

derivatives.zh: 由 popularity 去掉名词后缀 -ity 得到，义为「受欢迎的；大众的」
由 popular 加 -ize 构成，义为「使普及；使通俗化」
由 popularity 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不受欢迎」
由 popular 加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地；由民众」

senses.title: The state of being liked
senses.definition: the fact or condition of being liked, approved of or supported by many people
senses.definitionCN: 被很多人喜欢、认可或支持的状态
senses.example: Her popularity among younger readers grew with each new book.
senses.exampleCN: 随着每本新书出版，她在年轻读者中越来越受欢迎。
senses.why: The Latin noun popularitas first named the condition of being one of the people; being counted among them later turned into being favoured by them, and -ity fixed that favour as a state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 popularitas 最初指「身为民众一员」的状态；后来「被算作他们中间的人」变成「被他们偏爱」，后缀 -ity 又把这份偏爱固定成一种状态。

senses.title: The degree to which something is widespread
senses.definition: how widely a product, idea or activity is used or accepted by the public
senses.definitionCN: 某产品、观念或活动被公众使用、接受得有多广
senses.example: The popularity of online courses has changed how adults study.
senses.exampleCN: 网络课程的普及改变了成年人学习的方式。
senses.why: If belonging to the people can be shared by a habit as well as by a person, then the word can measure how far that habit has spread among them.
senses.whyCN: 既然「属于民众」既可以是人，也可以是一种习惯，这个词就能用来衡量这种习惯在他们中间扩散了多远。

senses.title: Public standing, often competed for
senses.definition: the position a person or group holds in public favour, especially when it is won, lost or competed for
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体在公众好感中所处的位置，尤指需要争取、会失去、会被比较的
senses.example: The two singers fought for popularity on the weekly chart.
senses.exampleCN: 两位歌手在每周榜单上争夺人气。
senses.why: Once liking can be counted it can be compared, and what can be compared can be contested, so the word shifts from a feeling to a ranking that people chase.
senses.whyCN: 喜欢一旦可以计数就能比较，能比较就能争夺，于是这个词从一种感受变成人人追逐的排名。

intro.en: Popularity is a Latin noun of shared citizenship that English turned into a measure of public favour.
intro.cn: popularity 本是拉丁语中表示「同属民众」的名词，英语把它变成了衡量公众好感的尺子。

items.en: Populus was the body of citizens, the crowd whose approval gave a word its weight.
items.cn: populus 指公民整体，是他们的认可给了某个说法分量。

items.en: Popularis meant of the people, and in Roman politics it described the side that courted them.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的，在罗马政治里指讨好民众的那一派。

items.en: Popularitas named the state of being one of the people, and by extension the favour that came with standing among them.
items.cn: popularitas 指身为民众一员的状态，进而指站在他们中间所获得的拥护。

items.en: French popularité carried the noun towards public favour, and English borrowed it in that warmer sense.
items.cn: 法语 popularité 把这个名词推向「公众好感」，英语借入时接受的就是这层更暖的意思。

items.en: Modern English made it countable and comparable, adding phrases such as popularity contest and ratings of popularity.
items.cn: 现代英语让它可数、可比较，于是有了 popularity contest 和各类人气排行。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the populus family and the noun built on it; the near-meaning group gathers words for public standing and renown.
note.cn: 形近组收 populus 词族及由它构成的名词；近义组收表示公众地位与名声的词。

entries.definition: Liked or accepted by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜欢或接受的。

entries.definition: To make something widely known or liked.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物广为人知或广受欢迎。

entries.definition: The act of making an idea or subject widely known.
entries.definitionCN: 使观念或学科广为人知的行为；普及。

entries.definition: A politician who claims to speak for ordinary people.
entries.definitionCN: 自称代表普通民众的政治人物；民粹主义者。

entries.definition: The state of being known by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 被许多人知道的状态；名声。

entries.definition: The opinion people generally have of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 人们普遍对某人或某物的看法；名声。

entries.definition: A person's rank or status in the eyes of others.
entries.definitionCN: 在他人眼中的地位或等级。

normalIntro.en: This word is the Latin noun of belonging-to-the-people, later narrowed into the amount of favour a person or thing enjoys.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语里「同属民众」的名词，后来收窄为某人或某物享有的好感有多少。

normal.en: Popularitas in Latin named the condition of being one of the people, not being liked; the modern sense is a later narrowing.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 popularitas 指身为民众一员的状态，而不是被喜欢；现代义是后来收窄的结果。

normal.en: Popularity is popular plus -ity, so the word names a state and never a person.
normal.cn: popularity 是 popular 加 -ity，所以它指一种状态，从不指人。

normal.en: You gain, lose or measure popularity because it is treated as a quantity.
normal.cn: 你会获得、失去或衡量 popularity，因为它被当成一个量。

normal.en: Popularity contest is a twentieth-century phrase from school and media life, where liking turns into a score.
normal.cn: popularity contest 是二十世纪从校园与媒体生活里来的说法，喜欢在那里变成了分数。

normal.en: Unpopularity adds un- to the same noun and keeps the same countable feel.
normal.cn: unpopularity 在同一名词前加 un-，仍然保留那种可计量的感觉。

abstract.en: A number climbing on a screen is a feeling that has been turned into a score.
abstract.cn: 屏幕上不断攀升的数字，是一种被换算成分数的感受。

abstract.en: To belong to a crowd and to be loved by it are two steps of the same walk.
abstract.cn: 属于一群人，与被这群人喜爱，是同一段路的两个台阶。

abstract.en: Popularity measures how far a thing has travelled, not how good it is.
abstract.cn: popularity 衡量的是某样东西走了多远，而不是它有多好。

examples.en: The band's popularity has grown since the tour.
examples.cn: 巡演之后，这支乐队的人气上升了。

examples.en: Critics questioned the popularity of the new format.
examples.cn: 评论者质疑这种新形式的流行程度。

examples.en: He won popularity by listening more than speaking.
examples.cn: 他靠多听少说赢得了人心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡普乐了题」——一道题在普通人里传开，人人都聊，就是 popularity：人气、普及。

root: 拉丁语 popularitas（公民身份、公众好感）← popularis（属于民众的）← populus（民众）；后缀 -ity 表示状态。

sensesIntro.en: From shared citizenship the noun narrows to being liked, then widens to how far something has spread, and finally to the standing people compete for.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从「同属民众」收窄到「被喜欢」，再扩展到「扩散得多远」，最后落到人们争抢的地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number on a screen climbing while the shopkeeper looks up at it again and again.
core.cn: 核心意象：屏幕上的数字不断往上跳，店主一次又一次抬头看它。

branches.en: a reader queueing for a signed copy
branches.cn: 排队等签售的读者

branches.en: a course catalogue that keeps growing
branches.cn: 不断加长的课程目录

branches.en: two names trading places on a weekly chart
branches.cn: 每周榜单上互换位置的两个名字

branches.en: a singer whose likeability becomes a ranking
branches.cn: 歌手的讨喜程度变成一项排名

branches.en: a format that spreads and is then ranked
branches.cn: 一种形式先传开，随后被排名

intro.en: A Latin noun of citizenship, its adjective and its suffix supply the stem. Here -ar belongs to the adjective, -ity builds this noun of state, and -ize would build the verb of making.
intro.cn: 一个表示公民身份的拉丁名词、它的形容词与后缀提供词干。这里 -ar 属于形容词，-ity 造出这个表状态的名词，-ize 则用来造表「使……」的动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the state of not being liked

definition_zh: 金属丝；电线；（电）电报；铁丝网；汇款
definition_en: a thin thread of metal, especially one carrying electric current, and by extension a telegram or a money transfer
core_image: 一只灰色的盒子背后垂出几根细金属线，指尖一碰有点发麻
scene: 拆开旧收音机，里面盘着几根细金属线，螺丝一松就弹了出来。 A loose wire behind the desk was the cause of the short circuit.
sceneCN: 这里 wire 是「电线、金属丝」（第 1 个义项：细细的一根金属线）；句意为桌子后面一根松了的电线导致了短路。盒子里盘着的那几根细线，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 金属丝；电线；电报；铁丝网

collocations.zh: 带电的电线；精力充沛的人

senses.title: A thin thread of metal
senses.definition: a long thin piece of metal, often bendable, used for holding, shaping or carrying current
senses.definitionCN: 细长可弯的金属条，用来固定、造型或导电
senses.example: The basket was made of thin copper wire.
senses.exampleCN: 这只篮子是用细铜丝编成的。
senses.why: The earliest sense is the drawn metal itself, a thread that could be bent into any shape.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项就是拉制出来的金属本身，一根可以弯成任何形状的线。

senses.title: A conductor of electricity
senses.definition: a metal thread covered with plastic that carries electric current in a building or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 外面包着塑料的金属线，在建筑或机器中输送电流
senses.example: A loose wire behind the desk was the cause of the short circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 桌子后面一根松了的电线导致了短路。
senses.why: Once electric current travelled along drawn metal, the thread of the craftsman became the artery of a house.
senses.whyCN: 电流开始沿着拉制金属走，工匠的那根线就成了房屋的血管。

senses.title: A telegram or a money transfer
senses.definition: a message sent along telegraph wires, or money sent between banks by message rather than in person
senses.definitionCN: 沿电报线发出的讯息，或银行之间以讯息而非现金方式转账的钱
senses.example: The news came by wire from the capital that same evening.
senses.exampleCN: 当晚消息就从首都用电报发了过来。
senses.why: Both messages and money moved along the wire, so the wire itself became the name of the service.
senses.whyCN: 消息和钱都沿着这条线走，于是线本身成了这项业务的名字。

senses.title: To install electric wiring
senses.definition: to fit a building or a device with the wires that carry power or signals
senses.definitionCN: 给建筑或设备装上输电或传信号的线路
senses.example: They wired the old house before moving in.
senses.exampleCN: 搬进去之前他们给老房子装了电线。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, meaning to provide a thing with this new kind of thread.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词，意为给某物配上这种新的线。

intro.en: Wire comes from Old English wir, the name of drawn metal worked into jewellery; the electrical sense arrived only in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: wire 来自古英语 wir，是拉制金属、用于制作首饰的名称；与电有关的义项到十九世纪才出现。

items.en: wir named fine drawn metal, used in rings and boxes rather than in machines.
items.cn: wir 指拉制得很细的金属，用于戒指与盒饰，而不是机器。

items.en: The word widened to bowls, strings and instruments, where a thread of metal holds or sings.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到碗、弦与乐器：一根金属线用来系住或发声。

items.en: The telegraph spread the word along its own lines, and a telegram became a wire.
items.cn: 电报让自己的线路把这个词传播开来，一封电报就被称作 wire。

items.en: Electric power gave wire its modern centre: the plastic-coated thread inside every wall.
items.cn: 电力给了 wire 现代的核心义：每一面墙里那根包着塑料的线。

items.en: Banks and later broadcasters produced wire transfers and wireless signals.
items.cn: 银行以及后来的广播人又造出了电汇与无线信号。

note.en: The first group holds look-alikes formed from adjacent letters, the second cables and threads of metal.
note.cn: 第一组收字母相近的形近词，第二组收电缆与金属线。

entries.definition: To clean with one sweep of a cloth.
Broad from one side to the other.
To pay for the use of something.
Thin and strong, like wire.
A thick bundle of wires or fibres.
A thin line of fibre, the picture behind wire.
A very thin strand of material.

normalIntro.en: Wire is short and thin like the thing itself, and its silent e keeps the long i.
normalIntro.cn: wire 像它所指之物一样短而细，末尾的 e 让 i 保持长音。

normal.en: Five letters, all narrow: the word looks like a wire on the page.
normal.cn: 五个字母一个比一个窄，这个词在纸上就像一根线。

normal.en: The silent e keeps the i long, as in fire and hire.
normal.cn: 不发音的 e 保持 i 长音，如 fire、hire。

normal.en: Wiry means thin and strong, so a wiry runner is built like wire.
normal.cn: wiry 意为瘦而结实，所以 a wiry runner 就像金属丝一样的人。

normal.en: Wireless drops the wire: signals travel without it.
normal.cn: wireless 去掉那根 wire：信号不再需要它。

normal.en: A telegram travelled on wires, so in old films a wire is a message.
normal.cn: 电报沿着电线走，所以老电影里 a wire 就是一封电文。

abstract.en: A faint hum heard through the box before it is opened.
abstract.cn: 盒子还没打开，就从里面听见一点嗡声。

abstract.en: A thread of copper catching a single point of light.
abstract.cn: 一根铜丝接住了一个光点。

abstract.en: A jump in the fingertip when the screwdriver touches the wrong spot.
abstract.cn: 螺丝刀碰到不该碰的地方时，指尖一跳。

examples.en: The fence is made of wire and wooden posts.
examples.cn: 这道篱笆由金属丝和木桩做成。

examples.en: Do not touch that wire with wet hands.
examples.cn: 不要用湿手碰那根电线。

examples.en: He wired the money to his brother the same afternoon.
examples.cn: 当天下午他就把钱电汇给了弟弟。

dict_mnemonic.text: fire 换成 w 开头，暖与光变成了细细的「电线、金属丝」。

root: 古英语 wir（拉制的细金属）→ 中古英语 wyr/wire → wire；同族有 wiring、wireless、wiretap。

sensesIntro.en: A drawn thread of metal becomes the carrier of electricity, then a channel for messages and money, and finally a verb of fitting such lines.
sensesIntro.cn: 一根拉制的金属线成为电的载体，再成为消息与金钱的通道，最后变成安装这种线路的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin bright thread of copper bending in the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根弯在手里的细亮铜丝。

branches.en: The metal branch: a basket woven from copper wire.
branches.cn: 金属分支：用铜丝编成的篮子。

branches.en: The current branch: a loose wire behind the desk.
branches.cn: 电流分支：桌后松了的电线。

branches.en: The message branch: news arriving by telegraph.
branches.cn: 消息分支：用电报传来的新闻。

branches.en: The verb branch: an old house fitted with lines.
branches.cn: 动词分支：给老房子装线。

branches.en: The carrier branch: whatever travels quickly takes the line's name.
branches.cn: 载体分支：走得快的东西都借用了线的名字。

intro.en: Wire takes simple endings and forms a rich family: wiring, wireless and the compound barbed wire.
intro.cn: wire 能接简单词尾，构成丰富的一族：wiring、wireless 以及复合词 barbed wire。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Old English; the Latin entry is a borrowed word for a metal thread.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属于古英语；拉丁条目只是借入的表示金属线的词。

items.example: It is the plain noun and verb.

items.meaningCN: 多根电线；第三人称单数

items.meaning: the lines installed in a place
to listen secretly on a line

items.example: The metal thread turned into a barrier.

definition_zh: 僵硬地；拘谨地；生硬地
definition_en: in a way that is rigid, formal, or not relaxed
core_image: 一个人挺直背脊、几乎不动地站着
scene: 他僵硬地鞠了一躬。 He bowed stiffly.
sceneCN: 这里 stiffly 是「僵硬地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他僵硬地鞠了一躬。

senses.title: Without bending
senses.definition: with a body that moves in a rigid and painful way
senses.definitionCN: 身体以僵直而吃力的方式活动
senses.example: He walked stiffly after the long ride.
senses.exampleCN: 长途乘车后，他僵硬地走着。
senses.why: This is the physical movement sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体动作的义项。

senses.title: Without ease
senses.definition: in a formal and awkward manner that shows no ease
senses.definitionCN: 以正式而生硬、毫不放松的方式
senses.example: She sat stiffly by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她拘谨地坐在门边。
senses.why: A body that will not relax behaves stiffly.
senses.whyCN: 不肯放松的身体，就会拘谨地行动。

senses.title: Coldly
senses.definition: in a cold and unfriendly way
senses.definitionCN: 以冷淡而不友好的方式
senses.example: He replied stiffly and turned away.
senses.exampleCN: 他生硬地回答，然后转身走开。
senses.why: Formality pushed far enough becomes coldness.
senses.whyCN: 拘谨到极点，就成了冷淡。

intro.en: Stiffly is stiff plus -ly, formed in modern English to describe rigid movement or manner.
intro.cn: stiffly 是 stiff 加 -ly，在现代英语中构成，描述僵直的动作或举止。

items.en: Stif meant rigid.
items.cn: stif 意为僵直。

items.en: Stiff widened to manner.
items.cn: stiff 扩展到举止。

items.en: The suffix -ly formed stiffly.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 构成 stiffly。

items.en: It described both bodies and manners.
items.cn: 它同时描述身体与举止。

items.en: It also named a cold way of speaking.
items.cn: 它也指冷淡的说话方式。

note.en: Stiffly is compared with look-alike words and with adverbs of awkward manner.
note.cn: 把 stiffly 与形近词以及表示生硬举止的副词作比较。

entries.definition: hard to bend
without fresh air
the people who work somewhere
in an official manner
in a clumsy way
without warmth

normalIntro.en: Stiffly is a body that does not bend, a guest who does not relax, and a voice that does not warm.
normalIntro.cn: stiffly 是不弯的身体，是不放松的客人，也是不升温的声音。

normal.en: He rose stiffly from the chair.
normal.cn: 他僵硬地从椅子上起身。

normal.en: She sat stiffly in the front row.
normal.cn: 她拘谨地坐在前排。

normal.en: The soldier stood stiffly at attention.
normal.cn: 士兵僵直地立正站着。

normal.en: He answered stiffly and left.
normal.cn: 他生硬地回答后就走了。

normal.en: The old man walked stiffly up the stairs.
normal.cn: 老人僵硬地走上楼梯。

abstract.en: A body can be stiff from cold or from pride.
abstract.cn: 身体会因寒冷发僵，也会因骄傲发僵。

abstract.en: What is held too straight cannot bow.
abstract.cn: 挺得太直的东西，弯不下腰。

abstract.en: Stiffness keeps feeling just out of reach.
abstract.cn: 僵硬，让感情总是差一点够不着。

examples.en: He bowed stiffly.
examples.cn: 他僵硬地鞠了一躬。

examples.en: He walked stiffly after the long ride.
examples.cn: 长途乘车后，他僵硬地走着。

examples.en: She sat stiffly by the door.
examples.cn: 她拘谨地坐在门边。

dict_mnemonic.text: stiffly 是 stiff 加 -ly，指身体「僵硬地」动作，也可指举止「拘谨地」、语气「生硬地」，常与 walk、sit、bow、reply 搭配。

root: stiff（僵硬的）加副词后缀 -ly；由身体的僵直，引申为举止拘谨与言语生硬。

sensesIntro.en: Stiffly means moving without ease, behaving without warmth, or speaking without softness.
sensesIntro.cn: stiffly 指动作不灵活、举止不亲切，或说话不生软。

core.en: A back held straight and still.
core.cn: 挺得笔直不动的背。

branches.en: An old man climbs one stair at a time.
branches.cn: 老人一级一级地爬楼梯。

branches.en: A guest sits far from the cushion.
branches.cn: 客人坐得离靠垫很远。

branches.en: A voice gives a short answer.
branches.cn: 一个声音给出简短的回答。

branches.en: The body sets the tone of the manner.
branches.cn: 身体的状态，决定了举止的基调。

branches.en: Formality at its limit sounds like coldness.
branches.cn: 拘谨到了尽头，听起来就像冷淡。

intro.en: Stiffly is fixed in form, built from stiff and -ly.
intro.cn: stiffly 形式固定，由 stiff 与 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 脖子僵硬让他动作迟缓。

items.example: A stiff breeze met the boat.
items.exampleCN: 一阵强风迎面吹向小船。

definition_zh: 传染的；有传染性的；有感染力的
definition_en: able to pass from one person to another, or able to make others feel the same
core_image: 一个人打一个喷嚏，旁边的人纷纷后退
scene: 孩子发烧不能去学校。 Measles is highly infectious, so she must stay home.
sceneCN: 这里 infectious 是「有传染性的」（第 1 个义项：疾病能传给别人）；句意是麻疹传染性很强，所以她必须待在家里。

pos.zh: 形容词：传染的；有传染性的；有感染力的

senses.title: Able to spread disease
senses.definition: able to pass a disease from one living thing to another
senses.definitionCN: 能把疾病从一个生物传给另一个
senses.example: The flu is most infectious in the first few days.
senses.exampleCN: 流感在最初几天传染性最强。
senses.why: The -ious ending means full of, here full of the power to infect.
senses.whyCN: -ious 词尾意为「充满」，此处即充满传染的力量。

senses.title: Able to be contacted by germs
senses.definition: carrying germs that can pass to others, said of a person
senses.definitionCN: 指某人身带可传给别人的病菌
senses.example: She is still infectious and should not visit the baby.
senses.exampleCN: 她仍然带菌具有传染性，不该去看宝宝。
senses.why: The quality can sit in the person rather than in the disease.
senses.whyCN: 这种性质可以落在人身上，而不只落在疾病上。

senses.title: Spreading cheer, not germs
senses.definition: spreading a feeling or quality quickly to others
senses.definitionCN: 把某种情绪或品质迅速传给别人
senses.example: His infectious good humour lifted the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他那有感染力的好心情带动了整个会议。
senses.why: The same spreading power is borrowed for moods, laughter and enthusiasm.
senses.whyCN: 同样的扩散力被借用于情绪、笑声与热情。

senses.title: Passing from mind to mind
senses.definition: spreading quickly among people, as of an idea or fear
senses.definitionCN: 指想法或恐惧在人群中快速传开
senses.example: The rumour was infectious and soon everyone believed it.
senses.exampleCN: 这则传言极具传染性，很快人人都信了。
senses.why: The adjective stretches further still, to ideas that spread without contact.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词还能进一步延伸到无需接触就传开的思想。

intro.en: Infectious adds Latin -iosus, full of, to infectus, the participle of inficere, to taint.
intro.cn: infectious 把拉丁 -iosus（充满）加到 infectus 上，后者是 inficere（沾染）的分词。

items.en: Inficere meant to put in or taint, with facere, to make, as its second part.
items.cn: inficere 意为放入或沾染，后半部分为 facere（做）。

items.en: The adjective infectiosus described air, water or a person full of contagion.
items.cn: 形容词 infectiosus 描述充满病源的空气、水或人。

items.en: The form reached French and then English, keeping the medical sense.
items.cn: 该形式经法语进入英语，保留医学含义。

items.en: Infectious was early applied to the plague and to fevers.
items.cn: infectious 早期用于瘟疫与热病。

items.en: The figurative use for laughter and enthusiasm appeared in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 用于笑声与热情的比喻义在十九世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the infection family; the near-meaning group holds adjectives of spreading.
note.cn: 形近组收 infection 词族；近义组收描述传播的形容词。

entries.definition: A disease caused by germs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「感染」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: To pass germs to someone.
Very valuable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「珍贵的」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Spread by direct contact.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「接触传染的」，强调接触。

entries.definition: Easily passed to others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，口语中义为「易传染的」。

entries.definition: Spreading fast among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「病毒式的」，常指网络传播。

normalIntro.en: The hooks join the -ious ending to the family, then follow the word from illness to laughter.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 -ious 词尾同词族相连，再随词义从疾病走到笑声。

normal.en: The -ious ending means full of, so infectious means full of the power to infect.
normal.cn: -ious 意为充满，所以 infectious 就是充满传染的力量。

normal.en: Contagious stresses touch, infectious stresses germs, and often both are used loosely.
normal.cn: contagious 强调接触，infectious 强调病菌，日常常混用。

normal.en: Infectious laughter is the phrase that shows the figurative side.
normal.cn: infectious laughter 展示了这个词的比喻一面。

normal.en: A person and a disease can both be described as infectious.
normal.cn: 人和疾病都可以用 infectious 来形容。

normal.en: Drop -ious and add -ion to get the noun infection.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ious 加 -ion 就得到名词 infection。

abstract.en: Infectious measures how far something can travel without moving itself.
abstract.cn: infectious 衡量的是某物不动却能把影响传多远。

abstract.en: Besides illness, an infectious person gives away their mood.
abstract.cn: 除了疾病，有感染力的人还会把心情分给别人。

abstract.en: The -ious suffix always suggests abundance: full of a force that seeks the next person.
abstract.cn: -ious 词尾总暗示丰盈：充满一种要寻找下一个人的力量。

examples.en: Chickenpox is infectious before the spots appear.
examples.cn: 水痘在出疹子之前就具有传染性。

examples.en: Her infectious laugh made everyone relax.
examples.cn: 她那富有感染力的笑声让所有人都放松下来。

examples.en: The doctor ordered him to stay at home while he was infectious.
examples.cn: 医生嘱咐他在具传染性期间待在家里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阴飞克死」——阴冷的病毒乱飞，把体弱的人克死，传染性极强。

root: 拉丁语 infectiosus = infectus（被沾染的）+ -iosus（充满）；词根为 inficere（放入、沾染）。

sensesIntro.en: Infectious begins as full of contagion, moves to the person who carries it, and then to moods and ideas that spread equally fast.
sensesIntro.cn: infectious 起初指充满病源，随后转指携带病源的人，再转向同样传播极快的情绪与想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sneeze that makes the whole room step back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个喷嚏让整个房间的人后退。

branches.en: DISEASE LINE: an illness able to pass on.
branches.cn: 疾病线：能传下去的疾病。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: a person still carrying germs.
branches.cn: 人体线：仍然带菌的人。

branches.en: MOOD LINE: laughter and cheer spread without germs.
branches.cn: 情绪线：笑声与欢乐无需病菌也会传播。

branches.en: IDEA LINE: rumours pass like a fever.
branches.cn: 观念线：传言像发热一样传播。

branches.en: SPREAD LINE: one force of passing things on.
branches.cn: 传播线：同一种把东西传出去的力量。

intro.en: An adjective in -ious built on the infection family, used for germs and for feelings alike.
intro.cn: 一个以 -ious 结尾、建立在 infection 词族上的形容词，既用于病菌也用于情绪。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -iosus was the Latin way of saying full of, and English kept it in countless words.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -iosus 是拉丁语表达「充满」的方式，英语在无数词里保留了它。

definition_zh: 拇指；竖起拇指表示赞许；（用拇指）翻阅
definition_en: the short thick finger at the side of the hand, or to press and turn pages with it
core_image: 一只手摊开，粗短的拇指单独朝上立着
scene: 旧书店里,他站在架前随手一页页翻过去,看有没有笔记。 He thumbed through the old book, looking for notes in the margins.
sceneCN: 这里 thumb 作动词，是「用拇指翻阅」（第 3 个义项：飞快地翻动书页）；句意为他翻着这本旧书，找页边有没有笔记。

pos.zh: 用拇指翻（书页）；竖起拇指示意搭车

derivatives.zh: 由 thumb 与 nail 复合，义为「拇指甲；缩略图」
由 thumb 与 print 复合，义为「拇指印」
由 thumbs 与 up 复合，义为「赞许的表示」

senses.title: The short thick finger
senses.definition: the short thick finger at the side of the hand, able to touch the other fingers
senses.definitionCN: 手侧粗短、能与其他手指相触的手指
senses.example: She held the coin between her thumb and forefinger.
senses.exampleCN: 她用拇指和食指夹住那枚硬币。
senses.why: The root meant to swell, and the thumb is the swollen-looking finger on the side of the hand.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「膨胀」，拇指就是手侧那根看上去鼓短的手指。

senses.title: The gesture of approval
senses.definition: in the phrase thumbs up or thumbs down, a sign of approval or rejection
senses.definitionCN: 用于 thumbs up 或 thumbs down，表示赞成或反对
senses.example: The project got a thumbs up from the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目得到了委员会的认可。
senses.why: The finger that can point up or down carries the whole vote in a gesture.
senses.whyCN: 那根能朝上也能朝下的手指，用一个手势承包了整场投票。

senses.title: To turn pages with the thumb
senses.definition: to press the pages of a book and turn them quickly, reading only briefly
senses.definitionCN: 用拇指压住书页快速翻动，只看个大概
senses.example: He thumbed through the magazine while he waited.
senses.exampleCN: 他一边等一边翻看那本杂志。
senses.why: The thumb both holds the book open and flicks the pages, so it became the verb for skimming.
senses.whyCN: 拇指既按住书页又拨动书页，于是成了「快速翻阅」的动词。

senses.title: A rough rule from experience
senses.definition: in the phrase rule of thumb, a rough method based on practice rather than theory
senses.definitionCN: 用于 rule of thumb，指凭实践而非理论得出的粗略方法
senses.example: As a rule of thumb, allow one hour for every site.
senses.exampleCN: 按经验，每个地点留一小时。
senses.why: A thumb’s width was once a handy measure, and a rough measure turned into a rough rule.
senses.whyCN: 一个拇指宽曾是方便的尺度，而粗略的尺度就变成了粗略的规则。

intro.en: Thumb is a native English word from a root meaning to swell, the same idea behind thick.
intro.cn: thumb 是英语本土词，源自意为「膨胀」的词根，与 thick「厚」同出一源。

items.en: The root described swelling or thickening, a good fit for the short, fat finger.
items.cn: 这个词根描述「膨胀、变厚」，正适合形容那根又短又粗的手指。

items.en: Old English þūma named the thumb, and the final -b appeared later under the influence of words like limb.
items.cn: 古英语 þūma 指拇指，末尾的 -b 是后来受 limb 一类词影响才出现的。

items.en: Middle English speakers used the thumb in everyday measure, so expressions of skill and clumsiness grew around it.
items.cn: 中古英语时期人们以拇指作日常尺度，关于灵巧与笨拙的说法便围绕它生出。

items.en: The verb thumb through, marking pages with the thumb, appeared once reading became common.
items.cn: 动词 thumb through 指用拇指标记书页，是阅读普及后才出现的。

items.en: Modern English keeps thumbs up in messages and images as well as in gesture.
items.cn: 现代英语让 thumbs up 既留在手势里，也进入消息与图片。

note.en: The first group gathers the thumb compounds and near spellings; the second compares finger words and gestures.
note.cn: 第一组收 thumb 的复合词与形近词；第二组比较手指类词与手势表达。

entries.definition: The nail of the thumb, and hence a very small picture.
The mark left by a thumb, used for identification.
The gesture or signal of approval, written with a hyphen.
entries.definitionCN: 表示赞许的手势或信号，带连字符

entries.definition: To hit heavily with a dull sound; one letter from thumb, other root.
entries.definitionCN: 重击（与 thumb 差一个字母，词源不同）

entries.definition: Any of the four long digits; the thumb is not counted among them in English.
entries.definitionCN: 手指（英语中拇指通常不计入 finger）

entries.definition: The finger next to the thumb, used for pointing.
entries.definitionCN: 食指（紧邻拇指、用于指物）

entries.definition: A digit of the foot, the body part parallel to the thumb.
entries.definitionCN: 脚趾（与手指对应的部位）

entries.definition: To move something with a quick movement of the finger or thumb.
entries.definitionCN: 轻弹（用指或拇指快速拨动）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the swelling root, the silent -b and the compound words.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「膨胀」词根、不发音的 -b，以及复合词。

normal.en: The b at the end is silent, so thumb sounds exactly like thum.
normal.cn: 末尾的 b 不发音，thumb 读起来就是 thum。

normal.en: The root meant to swell, and the thumb is the swollen finger.
normal.cn: 词根意为「膨胀」，拇指就是那根鼓起来的手指。

normal.en: Thumbs up and thumbs down need the plural -s even for one thumb.
normal.cn: thumbs up 和 thumbs down 即使指一只拇指也用复数 -s。

normal.en: All thumbs means the hands feel like fat thumbs: clumsy.
normal.cn: all thumbs 意为手上像全是粗拇指：笨手笨脚。

normal.en: Thumbnail is a thumb’s nail and, later, a tiny picture.
normal.cn: thumbnail 本是拇指甲，后来指小图。

abstract.en: Picture the short fat finger standing up alone while the rest fold away.
abstract.cn: 想象那根粗短的手指独自竖起，其余全收起来。

abstract.en: A thumb can measure, turn a page, hitch a lift and say yes.
abstract.cn: 一根拇指能量高矮、翻书页、搭便车，还能说「行」。

abstract.en: The clumsiest finger is also the one that shows approval.
abstract.cn: 最笨拙的手指，也是用来表示赞许的手指。

examples.en: He gave me a quick thumbs up through the window.
examples.cn: 他隔着窗户朝我快速比了个拇指。

examples.en: She thumbed through the report before the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会前她飞快地翻了一遍报告。

examples.en: As a rule of thumb, one cup of rice serves two people.
examples.cn: 按经验，一杯米够两个人吃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨姆」——萨姆总是竖起拇指夸人 → thumb 拇指

root: 古英语 þūma，源自日耳曼词根「膨胀、变厚」，与 thick 同源；末尾 -b 为后加。由拇指实体引申出竖拇指表态、用拇指翻页及「经验法则」等用法。

sensesIntro.en: Thumb starts as the swollen finger and then earns its keep in gestures, in page-turning and in practical rules.
sensesIntro.cn: thumb 起初是那根「鼓起的手指」，此后靠手势、翻页与经验法则立住脚跟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the short fat finger standing up alone while the others fold away.
core.cn: 核心意象：粗短的手指独自竖起，其余手指全收起来。

branches.en: The body part: a finger that can touch all its neighbours.
branches.cn: 身体线：能碰到其他所有手指的那一根。

branches.en: The sign: up for yes, down for no.
branches.cn: 手势线：向上为赞，向下为否。

branches.en: The action: pages flipped under the thumb.
branches.cn: 动作线：被拇指拨动的书页。

branches.en: The rule: a width of thumb as a rough guide.
branches.cn: 规则线：以拇指宽作粗略尺度。

branches.en: The hand measures as easily as it gestures.
branches.cn: 手既能打手势，也能当尺子。

intro.en: Thumb compounds with nail, print and up, and takes ordinary verb endings.
intro.cn: thumb 可与 nail、print、up 复合，动词则加普通词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，拉丁词条留空。

items.example: He is thumbing through a map.

items.meaning: a cap worn on the thumb
items.meaningCN: 顶针（原是戴在拇指上的）

definition_zh: 部分；片段；细分市场；分割
definition_en: one of the parts into which something divides, a short piece of speech or writing, a group of customers with similar needs, or to divide something into parts
core_image: 一只橘子被一瓣瓣掰开，摆在木桌上
scene: 她把橘子一瓣瓣掰开，分给围坐的孩子。 She divided the orange into segments.
sceneCN: 这里 segment 是「部分」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把橘子分成一瓣一瓣的。

senses.title: Natural part
senses.definition: one of the parts into which something naturally divides
senses.definitionCN: 某物自然分成的若干部分之一
senses.example: The orange breaks into easy segments.
senses.exampleCN: 这只橘子很容易分成一瓣瓣。
senses.why: Fruit and animals have natural segments.
senses.whyCN: 水果与动物都有天然的分节部分。

senses.title: Piece of speech
senses.definition: a short piece of speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面材料中的一小段
senses.example: She repeated a segment of the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她重复了采访中的一个片段。
senses.why: A broadcast or text is cut into segments.
senses.whyCN: 广播或文本常被切分成若干片段。

senses.title: Market group
senses.definition: a group of customers with similar needs
senses.definitionCN: 需求相似的顾客群体
senses.example: The ad targets a young segment.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告针对年轻群体。
senses.why: Marketers split buyers into segments.
senses.whyCN: 营销者把买家划分成不同细分群体。

senses.title: Divide
senses.definition: to divide something into parts
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成若干部分
senses.example: The company segmented its market.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司细分了自己的市场。
senses.why: The noun became a verb meaning to split.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示切分的动词。

intro.en: Segment comes from Latin segmentum, a cutting, from secare, to cut.
intro.cn: segment 源自拉丁语 segmentum（切下之物），出自 secare（切）。

items.en: Secare meant to cut.
items.cn: secare 意为切。

items.en: Segmentum named a piece cut off.
items.cn: segmentum 指切下来的一块。

items.en: English used segment for a geometric part.
items.cn: 英语用 segment 指几何上的一段。

items.en: The word spread to speech and biology.
items.cn: 该词扩展到言语与生物学领域。

items.en: Business adopted it for market groups.
items.cn: 商业领域用它指市场细分群体。

note.en: Segment is compared with similar-looking words and with words for parts.
note.cn: 把 segment 与形近词以及表示部分的词作比较。

entries.definition: relating to segments
divided into segments
the act of dividing into parts
one of the parts of something
a part of an economy or area
a share of something

normalIntro.en: Segment means a piece cut or divided from a whole.
normalIntro.cn: segment 意为从整体中切分出来的一块。

normal.en: An orange is easy to split into segments.
normal.cn: 橘子很容易分成一瓣瓣。

normal.en: A line segment has two endpoints.
normal.cn: 线段有两个端点。

normal.en: A radio show is made of segments.
normal.cn: 广播节目由若干片段组成。

normal.en: Marketers divide buyers into segments.
normal.cn: 营销者把买家分成细分群体。

normal.en: Segment shares the root sect, meaning cut.
normal.cn: segment 与表示「切」的词根 sect 同源。

abstract.en: Every whole can be seen as a set of segments.
abstract.cn: 每个整体都可以看作若干部分。

abstract.en: A segment is meaningful only against its whole.
abstract.cn: 一个片段只有对照整体才有意义。

abstract.en: Choosing your segment changes what you see.
abstract.cn: 选择哪个片段，会改变你看到的东西。

examples.en: The orange breaks into easy segments.
examples.cn: 这只橘子很容易分成一瓣瓣。

examples.en: She repeated a segment of the interview.
examples.cn: 她重复了采访中的一个片段。

examples.en: The ad targets a young segment.
examples.cn: 这则广告针对年轻群体。

dict_mnemonic.text: segment 由拉丁词干 seg（切）加 -ment 构成，本义「切下的一块」，引申为部分、片段与市场细分。

root: 源自拉丁语 segmentum（切下的一块），出自 secare（切），核心义「切分出来的一段」。

sensesIntro.en: Segment means a natural part, a piece of speech, a market group, or to divide.
sensesIntro.cn: segment 意为部分、片段、细分群体或分割。

core.en: A piece separated from a larger whole.
core.cn: 从更大整体中分离出来的一块。

branches.en: A natural division of fruit or body.
branches.cn: 水果或身体天然的分节部分。

branches.en: A short piece of talk or text.
branches.cn: 讲话或文本的一小段。

branches.en: A group of similar customers.
branches.cn: 需求相似的一群顾客。

branches.en: The act of splitting into parts.
branches.cn: 把整体切成部分的动作。

branches.en: The noun and verb share one cutting image.
branches.cn: 名词与动词共享同一个「切分」意象。

intro.en: Segment belongs to the Latin sect family of cutting words.
intro.cn: segment 属于拉丁词干 sect（切）这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin segmentum and secare are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 segmentum 与 secare 是历史词根。

items.meaning: a part cut from a whole
items.example: Each segment of the pipe fits tightly.
items.exampleCN: 每一节管子都接得很紧。

items.example: The worm has a segmental body.

items.exampleCN: 市场细分指导着这项计划。

items.example: The society had a segmentary structure.
items.exampleCN: 这个社会具有分段结构。

items.example: They dissect a fish in class.
items.exampleCN: 他们在课上解剖一条鱼。

items.example: The lines intersect at a point.
Bisect the square with a line.
items.exampleCN: 用一条线把正方形平分。
